# Refactor: consolidate the audit lease release/dispatch wiring found in the WL-0MWFJH3NW006F5GN review (dead monitor, duplicated availability read, unreachable retryAfterS, fleet version skew)

## Problem statement

The post-implementation review of the proxy audit-lease gate (WL-0MWFJH3NW006F5GN) left four structural/cleanliness issues in the lease wiring: the pane-close release/record is reachable only through a **disabled monitor** while the reaper — the only active close path — writes a separate record format; an audit dispatch attempt reads proxy availability **twice** (pre-check + admission); the `retryAfterS` cooldown on a saturated budget is **unreachable** because the pre-check refuses before admission's 429 arm ever runs; and a host whose pane predates the lease change silently runs availability-only admission (the exact cross-host race the lease gate removes) with **no version signal**. These are structural/cleanliness opportunities only — the audit-lease bug itself (WL-0MWJ7QONS0052HXX) is already fixed and stays the active path.

## Users

- **As a herdr downtime-worker maintainer**, I want one close path and one record format so a change to close/release behaviour (e.g. the next lease or budget tweak) touches one module instead of two drifting paths.
- **As an operator reading the dispatch/decision log**, I want a saturated audit refusal to name its `retryAfterS` cooldown even on the pre-check path, so I know when the tier re-checks without reading code.
- **As a fleet operator**, I want an old host (pane predating WL-0MWFJH3NW006F5GN) to be visible and refused for audit dispatch rather than silently reverting to the availability-only race.
- **As an audit reviewer**, I want the availability pre-check and admission to agree by construction (one read outcome), not by a second proxy GET that can race the first.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Single close path owns the pane-close record:** the reaper's per-pane close block (the only ACTIVE close path) writes the rolling-log `entryType:'pane-close'` record (host-budget release + proxy audit-lease release + pane-close record in one place), so `isNonTerminalCooldownActive` and the recent-dispatch view keep their input. The per-run `pane-close-ledger.jsonl` and the now-moot `alreadyClosedPaneIds`/`readClosedPaneIds` rolling-log guard are reconciled on one record. Regression tests drive the reaper (not `recordPaneClose`) and assert the rolling-log entry is written with the same fields `recordPaneClose` produces.
- **AC2 — One availability read per audit dispatch attempt:** the typed availability outcome read by the pre-check is threaded through the dispatch attempt into admission (`admitHostDispatch` already accepts the typed outcome as a seam option); admission no longer issues a second `readAuditAvailability()` GET and no longer re-maps `decideAuditAvailability` for the same candidate. A test pins exactly one read per audit candidate dispatch attempt.
- **AC3 — Saturated pre-check refusal carries the cooldown:** when the availability read reports `available:false` (the state a held foreign lease produces), the pre-check refusal derives `retryAfterS` from the held lease's `leases[].expiresAt` (epoch ms → seconds) and surfaces it on the decision entry exactly like the admission 429 arm does. No extra proxy calls; the acquire is still only attempted when the pre-check admits. Pinned with a captured payload test (held-lease availability → refusal with the derived cooldown).
- **AC4 — Fleet version skew fails closed:** workers advertise audit-lease support through the coordination check-in (additive capability/version field on the check-in/entry); the leader refuses audit dispatch to peers that do not advertise lease support. An old host (predating WL-0MWFJH3NW006F5GN) therefore cannot be the dispatch path for an audit — the availability-only race it would run is closed. Pinned with a test (peer without the capability → audit offer refused / not floated).
- **AC5 — No other behaviour change:** no existing dispatch, admission, cooldown or decision-entry shape changes beyond AC1–AC4. The full herdr suite stays green. (AC1's restoration of the pane-close cooldown input and AC4's fail-closed gate are the only intended behavioural deltas — both producer-approved.)
- **AC6 — All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md (lease protocol + close-path ownership + coordination capability), and any relevant wiki or docs-site entries.
- **AC7 — Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Impact

Fleet-wide audit dispatch becomes coherent again: one close path records every audit-lease release, one availability read answers the whole dispatch attempt, the saturated-refusal log names its cooldown, and a stale host can no longer silently reintroduce the double-audit race — so operators and reviewers trust the lease gate's guarantees without reading the wiring.

## Constraints

- **No net-new behaviour beyond AC1–AC4.** The four opportunities are structural consolidation; anything else introduced is scope creep and must be recorded as a linked work item (the review's own AC: each opportunity evaluated and actioned or declined — all four are now actioned with producer-approved options).
- The reaper remains the single active auto-close path — do **not** re-enable the pane-lifecycle monitor (`PANE_LIFECYCLE_MONITOR_ENABLED` stays `false`); the disabled monitor code is reconciled (deleted or documented as intentionally retained for redesign, per WL-0MWHWH6XL0025YX2's AC2 precedent).
- `AUDIT_BUDGET_SATURATED_REASON` / `AUDIT_BUDGET_UNKNOWN_REASON` / `AUDIT_BUDGET_UNAVAILABLE_REASON` spellings are shared with the proxy — never renamed.
- The lease acquire is still attempted ONLY when the pre-check admits (keeps "refused availability never churns a lease"); AC3 derives the cooldown from the READ outcome, it does not switch to acquire-on-every-candidate.
- The scheduling-hold/assignee-release and worktree disciplines in AGENTS.md apply unchanged (this is a refactor task — the implement skill's build → test → commit order applies).

## Existing state

- `PANE_LIFECYCLE_MONITOR_ENABLED=false` (`downtime-worker.constants.ts:735`) leaves `recordPaneClose` (`index.ts:1310`, the audit-lease release + rolling-log pane-close writer) reachable only from the disabled monitor (`downtime-worker.pane.ts:548`, gate at `downtime-worker.orchestrator-tick.ts:417`). The reaper (`runPaneCloseReaper` → `runReaper`) is the only active close path and writes only its per-run `pane-close-ledger.jsonl`.
- `getActiveAudit` pre-check (`index.ts:789`) reads availability and maps `decideAuditAvailability`; `admitHostDispatch` (`index.ts:1524`) reads it AGAIN moments later and re-maps it. Two proxy GETs and two decision maps per audit candidate.
- The 429 `retry_after_s` is carried on the admission refusal (`host-dispatch-budget.admission.ts:462`) and the orchestrator decision entry (`downtime-worker.orchestrator-dispatch.ts:734`), but the pre-check refuses BEFORE admission whenever availability reports `available:false` — exactly the state a held foreign lease produces — so admission's `saturated` arm and its `retryAfterS` deferral rarely run, and the pre-check refusal has no retry-after.
- Work Items panes run `npx tsx src/start.ts` and hold their module graph for days; a host whose pane predates the lease change runs availability-only admission with no version signal. The coordination check-in (`coordination.ts` v2 entries + `downtime-worker.coordination-checkin.ts`) carries `offers` but no capability/version field.

## Desired change

1. Consolidate the pane-close path on the reaper: the reaper's post-close block writes the rolling-log `entryType:'pane-close'` record (same shape `recordPaneClose` produces), releasing host budget + proxy lease + recording the close in one place; reconcile the per-run ledger and the `alreadyClosedPaneIds` guard onto one record.
2. Thread the pre-check's typed availability outcome through the dispatch attempt into admission so `admitHostDispatch` consumes the SAME read it would otherwise re-fetch — one proxy GET per audit candidate.
3. Derive `retryAfterS` on the pre-check refusal from the availability payload's held-lease `leases[].expiresAt` and surface it on the refusal/decision entry, so the saturated cooldown is reachable on the common path.
4. Add an additive lease-support capability to the coordination check-in/entry; the leader refuses audit dispatch to peers lacking it (fail-closed), closing the old-host race.

## Key Files:

- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — `recordPaneClose` (`:1310`), `runPaneCloseReaper` (`:1349`), `getActiveAudit` (`:789`), `admitHostDispatch` (`:1524`), `releaseAuditLease` (`:1610`) — the consolidation seams.
- `packages/herdr/src/pane-close-reaper.ts` — the reaper gains the rolling-log pane-close record alongside `releasePaneBudget`/`releaseAuditLease` (`:377–397`); ledger `writeLedgerRow` (`:259`) reconciled.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.downtime-resolvers.ts` — `readClosedPaneIds` (`:225`): the `alreadyClosedPaneIds` guard, reconciled or removed.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch.ts` (`:710` pre-check) + `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch-claims.ts` (claim pipeline → `admitHostDispatch`) — threading the one availability outcome.
- `packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.admission.ts` — the typed `auditAvailability` seam (`:23`, `:380–404` file markers); keep `decideAuditAvailability` as the single mapper.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.audit-availability.contract.ts` — `leases[].expiresAt` (epoch ms) is the AC3 cooldown source.
- `packages/herdr/src/coordination.ts` (`CoordinationEntry`/v2 entries) + `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.coordination-checkin.ts` + `downtime-worker.coordination.ts` (offer computation) — the AC4 capability field + leader-side refusal.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.audit-lease.ts`, `downtime-worker.audit-lease.test.ts`, `downtime-worker.dispatch-audit-lease.test.ts`, `audit-availability.cross-host.test.ts` — regression pinning for AC2/AC3/AC4.
- `packages/herdr/src/pane-close-reaper.test.ts`, `index.downtime-record.test.ts` — AC1 pinning (reaper writes the rolling-log pane-close record).
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — lease protocol section (close-path ownership, pre-check cooldown, coordination capability).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope creep into the four opportunities' neighbours** — mitigated by AC5 (no other behaviour change) and the linked-work-item rule: anything beyond AC1–AC4 is recorded as a child/discovered item, not folded in.
- **Coordination capability field is an additive protocol change** — old entries without the field must remain readable and an old peer without the capability must be refused for audits, never crash the leader; pin interop in a test (legacy entry shape + no-capability peer).
- **`alreadyClosedPaneIds`/`readClosedPaneIds` removal could drop the double-handle guard** — the guard is retained for historical entries (reaper comment says so); consolidating onto one record must keep the reaper idempotent across runs (verify with the existing `alreadyClosedPaneIds`-driven tests or an equivalent).
- **AC3 derivation edge cases** — `expiresAt` in the past (or a malformed lease entry) must clamp to a sane cooldown (≥0) and never throw on the pre-check path; the availability parser is already fail-closed.
- **Assumption:** the availability payload's `leases[]` actually carries the foreign held lease with `expiresAt` in the live proxy for the saturated case — pinned by the existing captured payloads and the live-proxy E2E (`downtime-worker.audit-availability.live.test.ts`); if the proxy serves `leases: []` while saturated, AC3 degrades to "no cooldown named on the pre-check refusal" and must be reported, not silently dropped.
- **Assumption:** AC4's fail-closed gate is an intended behaviour change for old hosts (producer-approved); the full suite must stay green with it.

## Related work

- **WL-0MWFJH3NW006F5GN** — the reviewed parent (proxy audit lease acquired before dispatch); the four opportunities originate from its review. The two-drift (pre-check-side vs admission-side) decisions there set the shape for #2/#3.
- **WL-0MWJ7QONS0052HXX** — the reaper lease-release bug (completed): the reaper stays the single active close path; this item is its architectural reconciliation (dead monitor, record formats).
- **WL-0MWFJ4LRH0025GGX** — the path/verdict fix (completed); base the availability read this item threads on the pinned contract.
- **WL-0MWHWH6XL0025YX2** — unified pane discovery/close logic (completed): the reaper-as-single-close-path precedent and the "delete or document retained" pattern for the disabled monitor.
- **WL-0MUMEKDK0008LKH8** — monitor disabled (completed); `PANE_LIFECYCLE_MONITOR_ENABLED=false` stays.
- **WL-0MWAMSK9H005BOHD**, **WL-0MWAMSCOP003R837**, **WL-0MWAMSDNW000SL0E** — admission choke point, fail-closed availability client, audit gate availability (completed); the seams this refactor consolidates.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Q1 (#1 dead close path — which record survives)? A: Consolidate on the reaper as the single close path — it gains the rolling-log pane-close record; reconcile the per-run ledger and the now-moot alreadyClosedPaneIds guard. B: drop the rolling-log writer (silently disables the non-terminal close cooldown). C: leave as-is." — Answer (producer): **A**. Source: interactive reply 2026-11-16 (comment WL-C0MWJBSCET0096D7W). Research: verified the rolling-log pane-close record feeds `isNonTerminalCooldownActive` (`downtime-log-markers.ts:316`) and the recent-dispatch view (`downtime-log-recent.ts:124`), so A preserves dispatch behaviour while B would disable the cooldown.
- Q: "Q2 (#3 retryAfterS — how to make the saturated cooldown reachable)? A: derive retryAfterS on the pre-check refusal from the availability payload's held-lease leases[].expiresAt (keeps 'refused availability never churns a lease'). B: demote the pre-check so the lease-acquire 429 is the single refusal point. C: decline." — Answer (producer): **A**. Source: interactive reply 2026-11-16. Research: availability contract (`downtime-worker.audit-availability.contract.ts:73–87`) pins `leases[].expiresAt` as epoch ms with a tolerant normaliser — the derivation source exists; admission's existing retryAfterS carry (`host-dispatch-budget.admission.ts:462`, `orchestrator-dispatch.ts:734`) gives the surface to mirror.
- Q: "Q3 (#4 fleet version skew — mechanism AND the AC1 tension)? A: advertise lease-support through the coordination check-in; the leader refuses audit dispatch to peers lacking it (fail-closed) — closes the cross-host race, but IS a behaviour change for old hosts, so AC1 must be relaxed for this case. B: local-only lease-seam-absent extension (old hosts still silent). C: observability only. D: decline." — Answer (producer): **A**. Source: interactive reply 2026-11-16. Research: coordination entries (`coordination.ts` v2, `CoordinationEntry.offers`) carry no capability/version today; the check-in (`downtime-worker.coordination-checkin.ts`) is the additive seam for advertising support, and offer computation (`downtime-worker.coordination.ts`) the refusal point.
- Q: "Fourth decision (#1 consolidation detail): does AC1 'no behaviour change on any existing path' apply at all given Q1-A restores a cooldown input the disabled monitor removed?" — Answer (producer): accepted implicitly with Q1-A — the cooldown input is RESTORED as intended behaviour (the feature exists and simply lost its writer when the monitor was disabled). Recorded as the documented AC1 behavioural delta. Source: interactive reply 2026-11-16.
- Duplicate-work detection performed: `wl search "audit lease"` / `wl search "pane close reaper"` returned WL-0MWHWH6XL0025YX2 (unified discovery/close — completed, disjoint scope), WL-0MWJ7QONS0052HXX (the reaper release bug — completed, this item is its architectural follow-up), and the completed gate/availability siblings — no overlapping open item. No duplicate found. Source: worklog FTS.
- Context verification: all four opportunities confirmed in the current tree — monitor gate (`orchestrator-tick.ts:417`), `recordPaneClose` sole writer of the rolling-log pane-close record (`index.ts:1310` via `downtime-worker.pane.ts:548`), duplicate availability reads (`index.ts:789` and `:1524`), pre-check-before-admission short-circuit (`downtime-worker.dispatch.ts:710`), coordination check-in without capability field (`coordination.ts` / `coordination-checkin.ts`).
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MWFJ4LRH0025GGX** – Audit admission still fails closed against the shipped proxy: wrong path and wrong available type (completed)
- **WL-0MUMM5FM5002CXUY** – Add regression tests for false-positive pane closes (completed)
- **WL-0MQOIBGIR006CWLR** – Add Background Task Runtime for Non-Blocking Operations (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: 0mumekdk0008lkh8, 0mwamscop003r837, 0mwamsdnw000sl0e, 0mwamsk9h005bohd, 0mwfjh3nw006f5gn (+443 more)
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: 0mumekdk0008lkh8, 0mwfjh3nw006f5gn, 0mwj7qons0052hxx, absent, ac1 (+408 more)
- `CLI.md` — matched: absent, ac2, accepted, accepts, acquire (+324 more)

---

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-11-16 (plan skill, pi): decomposed into 6 child work items (test-first order, deps wired):
  - WL-0MWJE9EWY003C8TQ (task) — Tests: pin the reaper's pane-close record and audit-lease release (AC1 test-first; prereq of the reaper consolidation).
  - WL-0MWJE9J2Y001VZ1M (task) — Reaper owns the single pane-close record (AC1 implementation; depends on the test child).
  - WL-0MWJE9IEH001R3P1 (task) — One availability read per audit dispatch attempt (AC2).
  - WL-0MWJE9N7L001V6XI (task) — Saturated pre-check refusal carries the derived cooldown (AC3).

# Tests: pin the reaper's pane-close record and audit-lease release

Test-first slice of WL-0MWJ7QYX0001KAQX AC1. Write these tests BEFORE the
consolidation in the sibling implementation child, so the shape of the single
close record is defined by a failing test rather than by whatever the
consolidation happens to produce.

## Context

The reaper (`runReaper` in `pane-close-reaper.ts`) is the ONLY active
auto-close path (`PANE_LIFECYCLE_MONITOR_ENABLED === false`). Today it releases
the host-budget ledger entry and the proxy audit lease, and writes a per-run
`pane-close-ledger.jsonl` row — but it does NOT write the rolling-log
`entryType: 'pane-close'` record that `recordPaneClose` (reachable only from the
disabled monitor) writes. That record is the input to
`isNonTerminalCooldownActive` (`downtime-log-markers.ts:316`) and the
recent-dispatch view (`downtime-log-recent.ts:124`), so the cooldown input is
currently missing in production.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Regression tests drive the **reaper** (`runReaper`, not `recordPaneClose`) and assert the rolling-log `entryType:'pane-close'` record is written for a closed pane, with the same fields `recordPaneClose` produces (`itemId`, `itemTitle`, `paneId`, `kind`, `outcome`, `reason`, `reasonCode`, `stage`, `closed`).
- The tests assert the proxy audit-lease release seam (`releaseAuditLease`) fires for a closed `audit` pane and does not fire for non-audit panes.
- The tests assert the reaper stays idempotent across runs: a pane already present in `alreadyClosedPaneIds` is skipped and no second record or release is produced.
- The tests assert a dry run and a failed close (`closePane` → `{success:false}`) write no `closed:true` record and release nothing.
- The tests fail against the current tree and pass once the sibling consolidation child lands (state the observed failure in the child's completion comment).
- The full herdr test suite stays green with this change (no other behaviour change).

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/pane-close-reaper.test.ts` — the reaper regression suite this slice extends.
- `packages/herdr/src/pane-close-reaper.ts` — `runReaper`, the seam under test.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log-entries.ts` — `PaneCloseLogEntry` shape the record must match.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.downtime-record.test.ts` — the `recordPaneClose` field expectations to mirror.

## Impact

The single close record gains a failing-then-passing pin, so the restored non-terminal close cooldown input cannot silently regress again.

# One availability read per audit dispatch attempt

Implements WL-0MWJ7QYX0001KAQX **AC2**.

## Context

An audit dispatch attempt reads proxy availability TWICE: `getActiveAudit`
(`index.ts:789`) reads it for the pre-check and maps it through
`decideAuditAvailability`; `admitHostDispatch` (`index.ts:1524`) reads it AGAIN
moments later and re-maps it. Two proxy GETs and two decision maps per audit
candidate, with the second able to race the first.

`admitHostDispatch` already accepts the typed outcome as a seam option
(`auditAvailability` in `HostBudgetAdmissionOptions`), so the read can be
threaded rather than re-fetched.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The typed availability outcome read by the pre-check is threaded through the dispatch attempt into admission (`admitHostDispatch` already accepts the typed outcome as a seam option), so a single read outcome answers the whole attempt.
- Admission no longer issues a second `readAuditAvailability()` GET and no longer re-maps `decideAuditAvailability` for the same candidate.
- A test pins exactly one availability read per audit candidate dispatch attempt (a counting stub seam asserts one call).
- The pre-check and admission agree by construction (one read outcome) and every fail-closed mapping (`audit-budget-saturated` / `audit-budget-unknown` / `audit-budget-unavailable`) is unchanged.
- The acquire is still attempted only when the pre-check admits (refused availability never churns a lease).
- No other dispatch behaviour change, and the full herdr test suite stays green with this change.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — `getActiveAudit` (`:789`), `admitHostDispatch` (`:1524`).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch.ts` — the pre-check (`:710`) and the `dispatchClaimedTier` call sites.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch-claims.ts` — where `admitHostDispatch` is invoked (`:414`-ish) and the input can carry the threaded outcome.
- `packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.admission.ts` — the typed `auditAvailability` seam; `decideAuditAvailability` stays the single mapper.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch-contract.ts` — `DowntimeHostBudgetAdmissionInput`.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch-audit-lease.test.ts`, `audit-availability.cross-host.test.ts` — regression pinning.

## Impact

An audit dispatch makes one availability observation instead of two racing ones, so the pre-check and admission can no longer disagree about the same candidate.
data.title: One availability read per audit dispatch attempt

# Advertise audit-lease capability and refuse old peers

Implements WL-0MWJ7QYX0001KAQX **AC4** (producer answer Q3-A: advertise
lease-support through the coordination check-in; the leader refuses audit
dispatch to peers lacking it — fail-closed).

## Context

Work-item panes run `npx tsx src/start.ts` and hold their module graph for
days. A host whose pane predates the lease change
(WL-0MWFJH3NW006F5GN) runs availability-only admission — the exact
cross-host race the lease gate removes — with no version signal. The
coordination check-in (`coordination.ts` v2 entries +
`downtime-worker.coordination-checkin.ts`) carries `offers` but no
capability/version field, so the leader cannot tell an old peer from a new
one before dispatching its audit offers.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Workers advertise audit-lease support through the coordination check-in as an additive capability field on `CoordinationEntry` (absent for legacy entries, so old readers/writers interoperate).
- The leader refuses audit dispatch to peers that do not advertise lease support (fail-closed): an old host (predating WL-0MWFJH3NW006F5GN) cannot be the dispatch path for an audit, so the availability-only race it would run is closed.
- A peer without the capability is refused for audits but its non-audit offers (implement/prep) still flow unchanged.
- Legacy entries without the field remain readable and an old peer is refused, never crashes the leader — pinned by an interop test (legacy entry shape + no-capability peer).
- The refusal surfaces on the coordination decision/attribution path with a distinct gate token (e.g. `lease-capability-absent`), so the leader's refusal is observable.
- This fail-closed gate is the only intended behaviour change for old hosts; the full herdr test suite stays green with this change.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/coordination.ts` — `CoordinationEntry` (`:111`) gains the additive capability field.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.coordination-checkin.ts` — the check-in writes the field.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.coordination-leader.ts` — the offer-admission loop (`:538`-ish, `rejectOffer` `:311`) refuses audit offers of peers lacking the capability.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.coordination.ts` — offer computation (`computeMostImportantItem`).
- `packages/herdr/src/coordination.test.ts`, `coordination-leader.test.ts`, `coordination-dispatch.test.ts`, `machine-coordination.test.ts` — interop + refusal pinning.
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — coordination capability paragraph.

## Impact

A stale host can no longer silently reintroduce the double-audit race: the fleet refuses audits through old peers instead of hoping they upgraded.
data.title: Advertise audit-lease capability and refuse old peers

# Saturated pre-check refusal carries the derived cooldown

Implements WL-0MWJ7QYX0001KAQX **AC3** (producer answer Q2-A: derive on the
pre-check refusal from the availability payload's held lease, keeping
"refused availability never churns a lease").

## Context

The 429 `retry_after_s` is carried on the admission refusal
(`host-dispatch-budget.admission.ts:462`) and the orchestrator decision entry
(`downtime-worker.orchestrator-dispatch.ts:734`) — but the pre-check refuses
BEFORE admission whenever availability reports `available:false`, which is
exactly the state a held foreign lease produces. So the admission `saturated`
arm and its `retryAfterS` deferral rarely run, and the pre-check refusal names
no cooldown at all.

The availability contract already pins `leases[].expiresAt` as epoch
milliseconds (`downtime-worker.audit-availability.contract.ts:73-87`), read
through a tolerant normaliser — the derivation source exists.

## Acceptance Criteria

- When the availability read reports `available:false` (the state a held foreign lease produces), the pre-check refusal derives `retryAfterS` from the held lease's `leases[].expiresAt` (epoch ms → seconds) and surfaces it on the decision entry exactly like the admission 429 arm does.
- No extra proxy calls: the acquire is still only attempted when the pre-check admits.
- Pinned with a captured payload test (held-lease availability → refusal with the derived cooldown), plus a test that the existing admission-carried `retryAfterS` surface is unchanged.
- A malformed or already-past `expiresAt` clamps to a sane cooldown (>= 0) and never throws on the pre-check path.
- If the live proxy serves `leases: []` while saturated, the derivation degrades to "no cooldown named" and this is reported on the child rather than silently dropped.
- No other dispatch behaviour change, and the full herdr test suite stays green with this change.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — `getActiveAudit` (`:789`) and the returned `DowntimeActiveAuditResult`.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.types.ts` — `DowntimeActiveAuditResult` (`:782`) gains the cooldown evidence.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch.ts` — `:710` pre-check consumption, refusal/decision shape.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.orchestrator-dispatch.ts` — the decision entry that carries `retryAfterS` (`:731`).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.audit-availability.contract.ts` — `AuditAvailabilityLease.expiresAt` (epoch ms).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.audit-availability.test.ts`, `audit-availability.cross-host.test.ts` — captured-payload pinning.

## Impact

A saturated audit refusal now names its cooldown on the common path, so an operator can tell when the tier re-checks without reading the code.
data.title: Saturated pre-check refusal carries the derived cooldown

# Dispatcher unevenly distributes downtime work across projects

## Problem statement

The downtime dispatcher is documented to share idle capacity across registered
projects by **global cross-project round-robin** ("no single project can
monopolise the downtime worker"), but measured dispatch history shows the
opposite: on each of the last three nights one project consumed roughly half of
all dispatches in long consecutive runs, while other registered projects with
live coordination entries were dispatched rarely or not at all.

Measured from every project's `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` on this
machine (rows with a `paneId`, i.e. dispatches that actually produced a pane):

| Night | Total | Distribution | Longest consecutive run |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2026-11-15 | 47 | AI_Hell 24, ContextHub 22, games_curator 1 | AI_Hell 11, ContextHub 9 |
| 2026-11-16 | 91 | games_curator 35, tce-the-rising 23, ContextHub 19, AI_Hell 14 | games_curator 5, tce-the-rising 5, 4 |
| 2026-11-17 | 96 | **SorraAgents 48**, tce-the-rising 16, games_curator 14, AI_Hell 10, ContextHub 8 | **SorraAgents 9, 8, 8, 6, 4, 3** |

Two further facts sharpen the picture:

- Every SorraAgents dispatch on 2026-11-17 was a **prep-tier** kind (21
  `intake`, 22 `plan`, 5 `risk-effort`) and none was `implement` or `audit`,
  whereas every other project's dispatches that day were dominated by
  `implement`/`audit`.
- The round-robin cursor (`~/.herdr/downtime/downtime-round-robin-by-root.json`)
  **is** being written — so this is not a repeat of the "cursor never wired"
  defect (WL-0MTQ2FGSK004CBRK) nor of the "charge at selection, not at
  dispatch" defect (WL-0MWFIZ8H5005FVNN). The residual behaviour is still
  unfair after both fixes landed.

## Users

- **As the producer**, I want idle machine capacity to rotate across every
  project that has dispatchable work, so that a project with a large backlog of
  one stage cannot consume the whole night while other projects' ready work
  waits, and so that standup reports are not dominated by a single project.
- **As a project owner (agent or human) watching a project go undispatched for
  a day**, I want to see *why* my project was skipped — a hold, a deep review
  queue, or a fairness defect — from the dispatch and decision logs, rather
  than guessing.
- **As the dispatcher maintainer**, I want the fairness rule to be enforced by
  the code path that actually chooses what to dispatch, with a test that fails
  when one project wins several consecutive slots while a peer has an
  admissible offer.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The dispatch selection path is documented and tested such that, when two or more projects have admissible offers and surplus capacity exists, no project is dispatched more than twice in succession; a failing-first test drives a coordination file with four roots holding interleaved admissible/held offers and asserts the bound.
- The residual bias is identified with evidence and one of the two candidate mechanisms below is either confirmed and fixed, or ruled out with recorded evidence: (a) rotation applies only to the tick's selected root, so when that root's offers are all held the leader falls through the remaining entries in raw coordination-file order; (b) prep-tier offers (`intake`/`plan`/`risk-effort`) are never held by the review-queue, CPU or audit-slot gates while `implement`/`audit` offers are, so a project with a large prep backlog wins every slot on a machine whose other projects have mature implement/audit backlogs.
- A per-project fairness metric is recorded on every dispatch decision (selected root, dispatching root, tick outcome, and the consecutive-run length for the dispatching root) so the distribution can be audited after the fact from `downtime-dispatches.log` or the coordination decision log without replaying logs by hand.
- Fairness accounting does not regress the existing overrides: critical-first dispatch, priority ordering, the review-queue depth gate, the audit slot minimum, the code-freeze split-by-skill, and the host-wide dispatch budget all behave exactly as they do today; each has a test asserting it still wins over round-robin rotation.
- The observed concentration is re-measured after the fix and reported on the work item: over a comparable window with at least three active projects, no project exceeds twice its even share of dispatches, and no project holds a consecutive run longer than the bound in AC1.
- New and updated tests cover the fairness invariant, the two candidate mechanisms, the overrides in AC4, and the fairness metric in AC3.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

The producer can trust that a night of idle machine time is shared across every project that has ready work, instead of one project absorbing half the night's dispatches while the others wait.

## Constraints

- **No new scheduler.** Fix the existing leader selection path (`selectLeastRecentlyServed` + the entry loop in `downtime-worker.coordination-leader.ts`); do not introduce per-tier cursors, a second ranking, or a new queue.
- **Preserve every existing gate.** Producer-review, attempt-budget, non-terminal cooldown, code-freeze, CPU saturation, audit slot minimum, in-flight and review-queue holds are sequential filters with established semantics (WL-0MWDDHVN and successors) and must not be relaxed, reordered or duplicated to buy fairness.
- **Fail-open fairness.** A cursor read/write failure, a lock timeout or a corrupt cursor file must never block or fail a dispatch; the tick degrades to today's behaviour.
- **On-disk cursor format unchanged.** `{ "<worklogRoot>": "<ISO-8601>" }` in `~/.herdr/downtime/downtime-round-robin-by-root.json`; no migration, so live machine state stays valid.
- **Hot path budget.** No additional `wl` spawns per tick; at most one extra coordination-lock acquisition per consumed offer.
- **Scope guard.** Any additional unfairness found outside the leader selection path (for example the own-backlog fallback tracked by WL-0MWAJ3RPX000HQIG) is recorded as a separate work item, not folded in.

## Existing state

- `selectLeastRecentlyServed` (`downtime-round-robin-by-root.ts`) is a pure read: unknown roots sort first, otherwise the oldest timestamp wins, ties broken alphabetically.
- The leader rotates **only the selected root** to the front of the entry list and then iterates the rest in coordination-file order; it returns after the first successful dispatch, so a tick dispatches at most one item.
- The cursor is charged only on a consumed offer (`isConsumedDispatchOutcome`), never at selection — deliberate, per WL-0MWFIZ8H5005FVNN.
- A root that is selected but whose offers are all held is never charged, so it stays first in the rotation indefinitely, and the fall-through order behind it is not round-robin.
- The decision log records per-offer rejections with gate tokens, but not the selected root, the dispatching root, or any run-length accounting; log rotation (500 lines per project) discards the evidence within hours, so past nights cannot be re-audited from the logs.
- Two adjacent defects are already fixed and must not be re-litigated: the cursor was never wired into the dispatch path (WL-0MTQ2FGSK004CBRK) and the post-dispatch charge was dead code (WL-0MWFIZ8H5005FVNN).

## Desired change

A leader selection path in which the rotation is applied to the **whole** ordered candidate set rather than only to the tick's first choice, so that a root whose offers are held cannot silently degrade selection to coordination-file order; plus enough recorded fairness evidence (selected root, dispatching root, run length) to audit any night after the fact.

**Key Files:**

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-round-robin-by-root.ts` — Selection is a pure read over the cursor; needs to expose an ordered candidate list (not just the single least-recently-served root) if the fix rotates the whole set.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.coordination-leader.ts` — The entry rotation, per-offer filter chain and dispatch loop (~490–810); this is where fall-through order is decided and where a run-length bound would be enforced.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.selection.ts` — `advanceRoundRobinCursor` and the shared `isConsumedDispatchOutcome` charge predicate (~619–666).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.offer-selection.ts` — `orderAdmissibleOffers`, the per-entry drain-aware tie-break that decides which of one entry's offers is tried first.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.head-scan.ts` — The registered-root sweep's own round-robin usage (~420–510); must obey the same fairness rule.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.log-coordination.ts` / `downtime-log-coordination.ts` — Coordination decision entry shape; needs the fairness fields from AC3.
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — *Fair scheduling: global cross-project round-robin* section (~4050–4130); states the guarantee that measurement shows is not met.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: fairness flapping the other way.** Forcing rotation can dispatch low-value prep work ahead of a mature project's ready `implement` item, and can slow a project that is the only one with work. Mitigation: the rotation only reorders *candidates that are already admissible*, and the existing priority/critical overrides still win (AC4).
- **Risk: cursor state carries no "held" information.** A root can look "least recently served" forever because holds are never charged; a naive fix would ping-pong between two starving roots. Mitigation: the four-root interleaved test in AC1 pins the behaviour.
- **Risk: log rotation destroys the evidence mid-investigation.** Mitigation: capture the 2026-11-15/16/17 per-project dispatch-log aggregates on the work item before changing code (the numbers in this brief are that capture).
- **Risk: the measured imbalance is partly legitimate.** A project genuinely holding all dispatchable work *should* be dispatched. Mitigation: AC5 re-measures with at least three active projects and compares against even share, not against zero.
- **Assumption (documented, not confirmed by a producer):** "fair" means an **even share of dispatch slots among projects that have admissible offers**, with critical-first and priority overrides preserved — this is the reading already stated in `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, so the brief does not block on it. See the OPEN QUESTION in the Appendix.
- **Assumption:** the per-project dispatch logs on this machine are a complete record of dispatches (they are written by the dispatching instance and agree with the round-robin cursor's accounting identity).
- **Scope-creep guard:** removing the own-backlog fallback (WL-0MWAJ3RPX000HQIG) and increasing per-project slot budgets are separate items; this item changes selection fairness only.

## Related work

Automated report (find-related skill):

### Related work items
- **WL-0MTQ2FGSK004CBRK** – RCA: herdr round-robin dispatch across multiple projects not working (completed)
- **WL-0MNGR0E6E000ZVEQ** – Fix AMPA start-work failure: CONTAINER_PROJECT_ROOT undefined (completed)
- **WL-0MTRBOU0Y002M2CX** – Downtime dispatches land in Podcast workspace instead of Dispatcher workspace (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: algorithm, dispatch, dispatcher, dispatches, distribute (+12 more)
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: dispatch, dispatcher, dispatches, distribute, evaluate (+9 more)
- `CLI.md` — matched: algorithm, dispatch, dispatcher, example, identify (+7 more)

Additional related work identified during intake (read directly, not part of the
automated report):

- **WL-0MWFIZ8H5005FVNN** (completed) — *Downtime round-robin: post-dispatch cursor charge is dead code, so one project can monopolise the dispatcher.* Same symptom class, adjacent cause (charge point); its own Risks section predicted this residual: "a root that never dispatches is never charged, so it stays first in the rotation indefinitely". This item covers what remained after that fix.
- **WL-0MTQ2FGSK004CBRK** (completed) — RCA that first found the cursor was never wired into the dispatch path. The wiring exists now, so this item is not a duplicate.
- **WL-0MTK1ILM2009QYB2** (completed) — retired the per-tier `sortEntriesByRoundRobin` second ranking in favour of offer-removal + re-offer; explains why rotation now lives only in the leader entry loop.
- **WL-0MWAJ3RPX000HQIG** (open, low) — whether to remove the own-backlog fallback; a related but separate fairness surface (only 2 of 96 dispatches on 2026-11-17 came from that path).
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — *Fair scheduling: global cross-project round-robin* and *Critical-first dispatch* sections define the guarantee this item measures.
- `docs/dev/release-dispatch-budget-evaluation.md` — the host-wide dispatch budget that must keep precedence over rotation.

Duplicate-work check: performed with `wl search` on `round-robin`, `fairness`,
`dispatcher`, `dispatch imbalance`. No open item covers this gap; the completed
items above are partial overlap only, so the ACs here are scoped to the residual
behaviour rather than rewritten from an existing item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

The work item was created by the producer and dispatched automatically by the
herdr downtime worker; no interactive interview round took place in this
session. No question was answered by a human in this session.

- Q: "What does 'fair' mean here — an even share of dispatch slots per project with admissible work, a share weighted by each project's dispatchable backlog depth, or a share weighted by item priority?" — Answer: **OPEN QUESTION** (no producer response in this session). Research: `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` states the intent as *global cross-project round-robin* with the explicit goal that "no single project can monopolise the downtime worker", and WL-0MTJ7IEI80055V2V's ACs describe alternating dispatch with a priority override. Working assumption for this brief: even share among projects with admissible offers, priority/critical overrides preserved. If the producer prefers backlog-weighted fairness, AC1/AC5 change but the rest of the brief stands.
- Q: "Is the imbalance the round-robin algorithm being wrong, or a genuine scarcity of admissible work on the other projects?" — Answer: **OPEN QUESTION** (self-answered as far as the evidence allows). Research: the two candidate mechanisms in AC2 are both consistent with the measured data; the 2026-11-17 split (all SorraAgents dispatches prep-tier, all other projects' dispatches implement/audit-dominated) points at gate asymmetry at least as much as at ordering. The brief therefore requires confirming or ruling out both mechanisms with evidence rather than assuming one.
- Q: "Should the fix also cover the own-backlog fallback and per-project slot budgets?" — Answer: **OPEN QUESTION**. Research: only 2 of 96 dispatches on 2026-11-17 came from `own-backlog-fallback`, and slot budgets are per-project configuration rather than a scheduling rule. Both are out of scope here and already tracked (WL-0MWAJ3RPX000HQIG for the fallback).

### Plan session — 2026-11-17 (agent `plan`, session `herdr-1794934614-3693221-32084`)

This planning run was dispatching-driven (no interactive producer in the
session), so no new interview round took place. The three OPEN QUESTIONs above
were re-reviewed rather than re-asked; each is dispositioned here:

- **Q1 "what does fair mean"** — **NOT BLOCKING.** AC1 pins the concrete
  behaviour (no project dispatched more than twice in succession while a peer
  has an admissible offer and surplus capacity exists) and AC5 pins the
  threshold (no project beyond twice its even share). The working assumption
  (even share among projects with admissible offers, overrides preserved) is
  the documented intent in `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` and is now
  exercised by the override-precedence regression tests. If the producer wants
  backlog-weighted fairness instead, AC1/AC5 change but the decomposition
  stands.
- **Q2 "algorithm wrong, or genuine scarcity?"** — **RESOLVED BY PLANNING,
  not by assumption.** This is exactly what the diagnosis child

  not pre-commit to a mechanism.

# Add startOn (earliest start date/time) to work items

## Goal

Give every work item a first-class **`startOn`** field — the earliest date/time at which the item may proceed — and make every CLI and Herdr-plugin **search surface filter out not-yet-started items by default**. Today scheduling is unenforceable: the only signal is a `[run-not-before 2026-11-19T10:25:00Z]` prefix baked into the title, which nothing filters on, which agents must parse by hand, and which pollutes titles permanently.

## Problem statement

Worklog has no structural scheduling dimension for temporal gates. Downtime-ordered work items encode their earliest-start date in the title text, and nothing enforces or filters on it. This means dispatchers can fire agents before measurement windows are valid, and restarts can silently void mid-flight windows.

## Users

- **Downtime dispatcher agents** — need a reliable `startOn` signal to know when an item is eligible for dispatch.
- **Human operators** — need `wl list`/`wl search`/`wl next` to respect temporal scheduling without manual date parsing.
- **Herdr worklist users** — need to see not-yet-started items read-only with a "not started until" marker.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Data model.** `startOn` is stored per work item as an ISO-8601 UTC timestamp, exposed in every JSON surface (`show`, `list`, `search`, `next`, `recent`, `in_progress`, dependency listings). **Default = the item's `createdAt`** when omitted, including on import of legacy JSONL/Git data that has no field (back-compat is the default, never "blocked").
- **AC2 — CLI authoring.** `wl create --start-on <ISO-8601>` and `wl update <id> --start-on <ISO-8601>` (offset accepted, normalised to UTC); `--start-on ""` clears it back to `createdAt`. Invalid values fail with an actionable message. `wl show <id>` is **never** filtered — an item is always retrievable by id.
- **AC3 — Default filtering in searches.** `wl list`, `wl search`, `wl next`, `wl in_progress`, `wl recent` and the equivalent JSON paths **exclude** items whose `startOn` is in the future. An explicit opt-in (`--include-not-started`, and/or `--starts-before <ISO>`) shows them, marked as not yet started in both text and JSON output. `in_progress` items are never filtered out (a started item has already started).
- **AC4 — Herdr plugin parity.** Worklist, dispatcher and audit-pickup queries apply the same default filter, so a future item is never dispatched or claimed by any Herdr worker. Surface not-yet-started items **read-only** in the worklist with a "not started until <date>" marker, following the existing held-items banner convention (WL-0MVR8FN1D002SCIR), and never clear or alter their state.
- **AC5 — Claim guard (defence in depth).** Setting an item to `in_progress` (or any claim path) on a future `startOn` is refused with a machine-readable reason (`start_on_not_reached`) unless an explicit, auditable override is passed; the override writes a comment naming the actor and the reason. The guard must not fire for `createdAt`-defaulted items.
- **AC6 — Migration and sync.** A documented, idempotent migration sets `startOn = createdAt` for existing items (`docs/migrations/`); `doctor` reports a mismatch; JSONL export/import and Git sync round-trip the field; cross-project edges (foreign ids) are unaffected; two-way sync never resurrects a stale value.
- **AC7 — Tests.** Unit and integration coverage for: default = `createdAt`; future-filtered out of every search surface listed in AC3; opt-in shows them marked; `--start-on` set/clear; claim refused and overridden; legacy JSONL import back-fill; sync round-trip; a frozen-clock test (no wall-clock flakiness).
- **AC8 — Docs and help.** `CLI.md`, `DATA_FORMAT.md`, `API.md`, `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` and the relevant skill docs updated; `wl create --help` / `wl update --help` describe the field and its default.
- **AC9 — Performance.** An index on `startOn` (or an equivalent query plan) so `list`/`search`/`next` stay within the existing benchmarks on the current store size; record the before/after figures.

## Impact

Users can now schedule work items to become available at a specific future time, ensuring that time-gated measurements and scheduled tasks are not dispatched before their measurement windows are valid.

## Constraints and non-goals

- **Non-goals:** a scheduler or queueing engine, recurrence, timezone UI, automatic re-anchoring of dates, calendar integration.
- Do not repurpose the existing `assignee` hold, `dependencies` or `blocked` status: `startOn` is temporal, dependencies are causal, the assignee hold is an operator claim. All three must compose (an item can be dependency-ready, unheld and still not-yet-started).
- UK English throughout; schema changes ship with migration + docs in the same change; no breaking change to existing JSON consumers (additive field, defaulted).
- Test discipline: the full suite through the project's test skill, and no direct test invocations outside it.

## Key Files

- `packages/shared/src/types.ts` — Add `startOn` to `WorkItem`, `CreateWorkItemInput`, `UpdateWorkItemInput`
- `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts` — Add `startOn` column to the `workitems` table DDL and bump `SCHEMA_VERSION`; include the field in every JSONL export/import row projection
- `src/migrations/index.ts` — Add the idempotent back-fill migration (`startOn = createdAt` for existing rows) and bump `CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION`
- `src/commands/create.ts` — Add the `--start-on <ISO-8601>` option, offset-accepted + normalised to UTC, defaults to `createdAt`
- `src/commands/update.ts` — Add `--start-on <ISO-8601>` (`""` clears back to `createdAt`); host the claim guard on the `--status in_progress` transition
- `src/commands/list.ts` — Default `startOn` exclusion plus `--include-not-started` / `--starts-before <ISO>` opt-in with a not-yet-started marker in text and JSON
- `src/commands/search.ts` — Same default exclusion + opt-in as `list`
- `src/commands/next.ts` — Default `startOn` exclusion (with opt-in) in the browse-feed selection
- `src/commands/in-progress.ts` — Default `startOn` exclusion, but never filter items already `in-progress`
- `src/commands/recent.ts` — Default `startOn` exclusion + opt-in
- `src/commands/worklist.ts` — Consolidated read (`db.list()` + shared browse feed) must apply the same default filter for every subset
- `src/worklist-selection.ts` — Shared browse-feed selection: carry the filter so `next`/`worklist`/Herdr agree
- `src/claim-hold.ts` / `src/claim-hold-read.ts` — Claim-path surfaces the guard sits behind; add the `start_on_not_reached` refusal and the audited override comment
- `packages/shared/src/fields.ts` — Add `startOn` to `VALID_FIELDS`
- `packages/shared/src/predicates.ts` — Add the shared `isNotStarted(item, now)` predicate (clock injectable for tests)
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — Surface not-yet-started items read-only with a "not started until <date>" marker, following `dispatch-window-hold.ts`'s banner convention
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatch-window-hold.ts` — Reference implementation for the read-only banner; extend or mirror for not-yet-started items
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch-filter.ts` — Filter out not-yet-started items from the Herdr list-head dispatch pipeline
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.gates.ts` — Add the `startOnNotReached` gate (never dispatch a future item)
- `src/commands/export.ts` / `src/commands/import.ts` — Round-trip `startOn`; legacy rows without it import as `createdAt`
- `src/doctor/` — Add a mismatch check (`startOn` missing ≠ `createdAt`) to `wl doctor`
- `docs/CLI.md` — Document `--start-on`, `--include-not-started`, `--starts-before`
- `docs/DATA_FORMAT.md` — Document the `startOn` field and its `createdAt` default
- `docs/API.md` — Document `startOn` in every JSON surface
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — Document `startOn` scheduling and the claim guard
- `docs/migrations/` — Add the migration note

## Existing state

- No `startOn` field exists anywhere in the codebase.
- Current practice: `[run-not-before YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ]` prefix in item titles, parsed manually by agents.
- Items created 2026-11-18 from the `llm` abort-class remediation chain (`LP-0MWM0B7IQ008W2FP`) encode scheduling in titles.

## Definition of done

A `llm`-style dated work item created with `--start-on 2026-11-19T10:25:00Z` is invisible to `wl next`, `wl search`, `wl list` and the Herdr worklist until that instant, visible with `--include-not-started`, retrievable by id, claimable only after the instant (or by explicit audited override), and survives export/import and a restart unchanged.

## Related work

- LP-0MWM0B7IQ008W2FP — `llm` abort-class remediation chain (explicitly scheduled by title dates; blocked on this feature)
- WL-0MVR8FN1D002SCIR — Held-items banner convention (reference for Herdr worklist UI marker)

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk (scope creep):** `startOn` invites adjacent scheduling features (recurrence, calendar, timezone UI, auto re-anchoring). Mitigation: non-goals are explicit above; extra opportunities become linked work items, not scope.
- **Risk (silent behaviour change):** filtering by default could hide items an operator expects to see. Mitigation: the default is `createdAt`, so every existing item is already "started" and stays visible — the filter only bites on newly authored dates; `--include-not-started` is the escape hatch and not-yet-started items are surfaced read-only in the worklist rather than hidden.
- **Risk (clock flakiness):** future/past comparisons against wall-clock make tests non-deterministic. Mitigation: inject the clock through the shared predicate; AC7 requires a frozen-clock test.
- **Risk (sync resurrection):** a two-way sync could resurrect a stale `startOn` from the remote. Mitigation: AC6 requires two-way sync to never resurrect a stale value, covered by a sync round-trip test.
- **Risk (performance regression):** a non-indexed `startOn` predicate on every search surface could slow `list`/`search`/`next`. Mitigation: AC9 requires an index (or an equivalent query plan) with recorded before/after benchmarks.
- **Assumption:** `createdAt` is always present and non-empty on every existing row, so "default = `createdAt`" needs no fallback beyond the migration back-fill.
- **Assumption:** `startOn` composes with existing gates (dependency readiness, assignee hold, `needsProducerReview`) rather than replacing any of them — the new filter is an additional sequential filter.
- **Assumption:** the downtime dispatcher and `llm`-style dated items are the first consumers; no other project relies on title-embedded dates programmatically.

- No clarifying questions — the seed context (work item description) provides sufficient detail for a clear brief. The description was authored by the downtime dispatcher and contains a complete spec with 9 acceptance criteria, constraints, and definition of done.

read/write path → migration → export/import → sync → `doctor` → tests →
migration note; slice 4 goes option parsing → shared filter → text renderer →
JSON contract → docs. No slice is a single horizontal layer.

**Between phases:** review the next slice's description and refresh it against
what the previous slice actually shipped (notably the concrete `startOn`
storage invariant from slice 2, which informs slices 4–6).

### Plan-approval gate

Not requested: effort Large (not Extra Large) and risk Medium (not High/Severe).

## Review stages (automated, completed)

1. **Requirements & AC alignment review** — all nine parent ACs trace to a
   child; nothing invented. Applied: each child now restates its covering
   parent ACs verbatim under a level-3 subheading inside its `## Acceptance
   Criteria` section, so parent/child coverage is exact rather than
   approximate.
2. **Completeness review** — every child has Goal, Context, Acceptance
   Criteria, Key Files, Dependencies and Deliverables. Corrected five Key Files
   paths that did not exist in the tree: `packages/shared/src/test-utils/clock.ts`
   → `tests/helpers/frozen-clock.ts`; `src/commands/create.test.ts` and
   `src/commands/update.test.ts` → `tests/cli/create-start-on.test.ts` and
   `tests/cli/update-start-on.test.ts` (this repo colocates `packages/*` tests
   but keeps `src/commands/*` tests under `tests/cli/`); `packages/herdr/src/claim.ts`
   → `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.claim.ts`. **Note (pre-existing, not fixed
   here):** children use the `## Key Files` heading because that is what the
   tree's own consumers parse (`src/commands/helpers.ts::extractFilePaths`,
   `src/audit-fingerprint.ts::extractKeyFiles`) and what the parent item uses;
   the plan skill's `validate_key_files_format` only recognises a bold
   `**Key Files:**` marker, so it no-ops on this repo's convention. Reported,
   not silently rewritten.
3. **Sequencing & dependencies review** — the graph is acyclic and every edge
   is actionable; test/verification capability (slice 1) precedes all
   implementation and the documentation/perf slice runs last.
4. **Scope sizing review** — seven deliverable increments across a ~149h Large
   estimate (≈15–25h each); slice 2 is the largest but cannot be split without
   producing a horizontally-broken state (a column without its migration).
5. **Acceptance & testability review** — converted two either/or ACs into
   definitive, testable ones: a bare date is now explicitly **rejected**, and
   the not-yet-started text marker / Herdr banner copy are now specified
   concretely (mirroring `[held: N by Map]`).
6. **Polish & handoff review** — UK English, consistent headings, checkboxed
   ACs, explicit non-goals per slice.

**AC coverage review** (`tree_coverage`): `proceed` — 9/9 parent ACs covered,
coverage 100%, zero unresolvable conflicts, zero warnings. No covering children
were auto-created (none needed).

## Decisions taken (reversible)

- **D1 — `startOn` is always stored populated** as the effective instant
  (`startOn ?? createdAt`); a `NULL` on a legacy row reads as `createdAt`. This
  keeps the default-filter query a single-column comparison so the `startOn`
  index (AC9) is actually used, instead of a `COALESCE(startOn, createdAt)`
  expression that defeats a plain index.
- **D2 — unparseable `startOn` is treated as *started* (fail-open).** AC1 pins
  the back-compat default as "never blocked"; `startOn` is a scheduling gate,
  not a security control, so an unreadable value must not hide an item. AC2's
  authoring validation means this should be unreachable.
- **D3 — a bare date (`2026-11-19`) is rejected.** Its timezone would be
  ambiguous and AC2 requires invalid values to fail actionably.
- **D4 — the refusal token is `start_on_not_reached`** (AC5). The override flag
  is proposed as `--force-start-on <reason>`; the implementer may rename it if
  the CLI's flag conventions demand, provided it stays auditable.
- **D5 — the boundary is inclusive:** `startOn == now` counts as *started*.
- **D6 — both opt-ins ship:** `--include-not-started` **and** `--starts-before
  <ISO>` (AC3 allows "and/or"), composing as "not started AND starting before
  `<ISO>`". `--starts-before` is what a scheduler-facing caller actually wants.
- **D7 — child priorities:** `high` for the six functional slices, `medium` for
  the docs/perf slice. The parent stays `critical`.
- **D8 — no standalone horizontal "tests" children.** Each slice owns its own
  tests; slice 1 owns the shared frozen-clock harness so the test-first
  requirement is met structurally.

## Open questions (non-blocking — producer may override)

- **OPEN QUESTION (for the Producer).** Should the claim-guard override be
  restricted to named actors (e.g. the producer sentinel `Map`) or open to any
  agent? *Proposed default:* open to any actor, with the override comment
  recording the actor and reason as the audit trail (AC5). Not blocking —
  slice 5 can ship the permissive form and tighten later.
- **OPEN QUESTION (for the Producer).** Does `startOn` need to appear in the TUI
  worklist (`packages/tui`) as well as Herdr? AC4 scopes Herdr only, so the TUI
  is out of scope by omission. *Proposed default:* out of scope; raise a
  separate work item if wanted. Not blocking.
- **OPEN QUESTION (for the Producer).** Should existing `[run-not-before …]`
  title prefixes be rewritten once `startOn` exists? *Proposed default:* no —
  automatic re-anchoring is an explicit non-goal; the `llm` abort-class chain
  (`LP-0MWM0B7IQ008W2FP`) re-authors its own titles when it unblocks. Not
  blocking.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interactive producer was available during this planning run (the session was
dispatched by the downtime worker), and the parent's intake brief is complete:
it carries nine acceptance criteria, explicit non-goals, constraints, risks,
assumptions and a definition of done. Rather than stall, the three genuinely
open design choices were resolved to documented defaults (above) and are
recorded here with explicit preferred options so a producer can confirm or
reverse them cheaply.

- **Q1 (plan → producer).** "Should the claim-guard override be restricted to
  named actors, or open to any agent that passes an explicit flag?"
  **Answer:** not answered by a producer. *Plan agent's proposed default:* open
  to any actor; the override writes a comment naming the actor and reason, so
  it is auditable either way. Evidence: AC5 requires only "an explicit,
  auditable override … naming the actor and the reason". Status: **proposed,
  non-blocking.**
- **Q2 (plan → producer).** "Is the TUI worklist in scope for the
  not-yet-started marker, or is Herdr parity sufficient?"
  **Answer:** not answered by a producer. *Plan agent's proposed default:*
  Herdr only. Evidence: AC4 names "Worklist, dispatcher and audit-pickup
  queries" in the Herdr plugin and does not mention `packages/tui`. Status:
  **proposed, non-blocking.**
- **Q3 (plan → producer).** "Should existing `[run-not-before …]` title prefixes
  be rewritten as part of this work?" **Answer:** not answered by a producer.
  *Plan agent's proposed default:* no rewrite. Evidence: the parent's non-goals
  exclude "automatic re-anchoring of dates", and
  `LP-0MWM0B7IQ008W2FP` is the consumer that owns its own titles. Status:
  **proposed, non-blocking.**

Research performed (no questions raised, recorded for traceability):

- **Duplicate-work detection** — `wl search startOn`, `wl search run-not-before`
  and `wl list startOn` each return only this parent item. No overlapping
  completed or in-flight item exists, so nothing was closed or rewritten as a
  duplicate.
- **Choke-point confirmation** — `src/worklist-selection.ts::selectBrowseFeed`
  is the shared browse-feed path used by `wl next`, `wl worklist` and the Herdr
  fetchers; the intake comment on this item flags it as the single place AC4
  must be satisfied. Verified by reading the module.
- **Reference convention** — `packages/herdr/src/dispatch-window-hold.ts`
  (WL-0MVR8FN1D002SCIR) supplies the read-only header-count + banner pattern
  (`[held: N by Map]`), reused verbatim in shape for `[not started: N]`.
- **Gate-token pattern** — `ClassifyGateToken` in
  `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.offer-attribution.ts` is the existing
  stable-token union that `classifyItemForDispatchDetail` returns; the
  `startOnNotReached` gate extends it rather than introducing a parallel
  mechanism.
- **Schema state** — `SCHEMA_VERSION = 9` in
  `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts` and `CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION = '9'`
  in `src/migrations/index.ts` must be bumped together in slice 2.

## Plan: changelog

- Plan run started (session `herdr-1795026172-1600543-23749`): pre-check →
  `plan`; approval gate → not requested.
- Seven child work items created under this parent (test-first order), then
  dependency edges wired: `1→2→3`, `4,5→{1,2,3}`, `6→{1,2,4}`, `7→{3,4,5,6}`.
- Five incorrect Key Files paths corrected across slices 1, 3 and 5.
- Two vague either/or acceptance criteria made definitive (bare-date rejection;
  concrete text marker and Herdr banner copy).
- Parent acceptance criteria restated verbatim inside each child's AC section;
  AC coverage review re-run from `auto_close` (55.6%) to `proceed` (100%).
- Stage advanced to `plan_complete`.

# Intake Brief — Priority-first section ordering for the sprint view

## Problem statement

In the herdr sprint view (`f-s-s` → `/wl`) and the core `wl next --groups` output, sections are bucketed by **stage**, not priority, so a medium-priority `plan_complete` item renders above a high-priority `idea` item. Priority is only ever a *within-section* sort key.

## Users

- **Producers browsing the sprint view** (`f-s-s`).
  - *As a producer, I want high-priority work shown above medium-priority work regardless of its stage, so the top of my sprint view is genuinely the most urgent work.*
- **CLI users running `wl next --groups`** — the same ordering contract applies, so the fix must land in both copies.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts` → `assignItemGroups` buckets by stage: `Critical Group N` → `Group N` (in-progress / `plan_complete` / `intake_complete`) → `Idea` → `Other` → `In Review`.
- `src/commands/grouping.ts` → `assignItemGroups` is the core duplicate used by `wl next --groups`; both module headers state the copies must be kept in sync.
- `compareGroupableItems` already sorts priority-first *within* a section (WL-0MVVLBTTP003Y4XO), but the section boundaries themselves are stage-derived.
- `packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.ts` → `selectWorkItems` slices the non-mandatory `others` in raw `wl next` score order before truncating to `othersLimit`. Because `computeScore` (`packages/shared/src/database/sort.ts`) awards +3500 to a fresh audit-not-ready item, a medium (2000 + 3500 = 5500) outranks a plain high (3000) — so a medium can be *selected* while a high is cut from the sprint window entirely.
- Precedent: `Bubble up critical items (WL-0MR1COW20005IO1C)` introduced the priority-band-first mechanism for `critical` only. This item generalises it to every non-critical band.

## Desired change

Order sections by priority band first; use stage/state only as the intra-band tie-breaker and for selection tie-breaking.

1. **Bucket order** — priority band first: `critical` → `high` → `medium` → `low`. Within a band the stage sub-order is the tie-breaker: `status === 'in-progress'` → `plan_complete` → `intake_complete` → `idea` → other.
2. **`In Review` stays pinned last** — a single global section rendered after every band; it never moves into its own priority band (explicit exception — the review queue is mandatory and always shown).
3. **File-path conflict grouping preserved within each band** — greedy first-fit, max 3 file-path groups per band-section; items with no Key Files remain singleton groups. "Two items sharing a Key File never share a file-path group" continues to hold *within* a band.
4. **Selection** — the non-mandatory `others` slice is ordered priority-first, with the existing `wl next` score as the tie-break, *before* the `othersLimit` truncation. Highs can therefore never be displaced by mediums when more highs exist than the window allows.
5. **Labels** — extend the existing `Critical Group N` scheme to `High Group N` / `Medium Group N` / `Low Group N` with each band's stage sub-sections, and `In Review` last. The core `wl next --groups` output changes with herdr (deliberate; both copies in lockstep).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A mixed set of `high@idea` and `medium@plan_complete` items is regrouped so every high item's group number is lower than every medium item's — the inversion is gone.
- Section order is `critical` → `high` → `medium` → `low` → `In Review`, independent of stage.
- Within a priority band the stage sub-order is `status='in-progress'` → `plan_complete` → `intake_complete` → `idea` → other; stage never reorders across priorities.
- `In Review` is rendered as the final single section regardless of the priority of its members.
- Two items in the same priority band sharing a Key File never share a file-path group; the 3-file-path-group cap applies per band-section; items with no Key Files remain singleton groups.
- With 5 high and 2 medium non-mandatory items and `othersLimit = 3`, all 3 selected `others` are high-priority — no medium displaces a high.
- The always-show mandatory guarantee is unchanged: every `critical`, `in-progress`, `blocked` and `completed`/`in_review` item is still selected regardless of the window.
- Grouping remains a pure function of item content — no dependence on `updatedAt`, arrival order, or pin-map insertion order.
- Section labels follow the band scheme: `Critical Group N`, `High Group N`, `Medium Group N`, `Low Group N`; no non-critical section is labelled plain `Group N`.
- `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts` and `src/commands/grouping.ts` implement the identical order and stay in sync; `wl next --groups` reflects the new section order.
- Existing grouping/selection tests are updated and new tests cover: the high@idea vs medium@plan_complete inversion (both copies), the `In Review` pin, per-band file-path grouping, and the selection-truncation case.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

Producers see the most urgent work at the top of the sprint view regardless of what stage each item is in, instead of medium-priority in-progress-stage work pushing high-priority ideas out of sight.

## Constraints

- `packages/shared/src/database/sort.ts` (`computeScore`) is **not** changed — only its consumers (grouping and selection).
- Blocker pinning (WL-0MW7YJYS5009H7WC) must keep working: a pinned blocker still shares the blocked item's group and sorts immediately after it.
- Expand/`childCount` reachability, root substitution and the mandatory always-show set are untouched.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Copy drift** — `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts` and `src/commands/grouping.ts` are hand-synchronised; a partial change leaves `wl next --groups` disagreeing with the sprint view. Mitigation: change both in one commit and assert the same contract in both suites.
- **Blocker-pinning regression** — the pinned-blocker group override interacts with band partitioning; a pinned blocker must stay in its blocked item's group *and* inherit that item's band. Mitigation: keep the existing pinning tests green and add a cross-band case.
- **Test churn** — roughly 2,300 lines of existing grouping/selection tests encode the old stage-first order and must be rewritten rather than extended; a careless rewrite can bake in the new bug. Mitigation: derive expectations from this brief's contract, not from current output.
- **Scope creep** — consolidating the two grouping copies into one shared module, or changing `computeScore`, is out of scope here; file as separate work items.
- **Assumption** — `others` arrive from `wl next` already score-ordered, so the change is a stable priority-first re-sort with score as tie-break, not a full re-score.

## **Key Files:**

- `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts` — `assignItemGroups` band-first bucketing; `compareGroupableItems` intra-band tie-break.
- `src/commands/grouping.ts` — the core `wl next --groups` duplicate; must match herdr exactly.
- `packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.ts` — `selectWorkItems` priority-first ordering of the `others` slice before truncation.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.root-substitution.ts` — selection tail; verify pin/substitution interaction.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — sprint-view render path (verification only).

## Related work

- `Bubble up critical items (WL-0MR1COW20005IO1C)` — the completed precedent that added the `Critical Group N` band; this item generalises the mechanism to all bands.
- WL-0MVVLBTTP003Y4XO — made priority the primary *within-group* sort key.
- WL-0MW7YJYS5009H7WC — blocker pinning (group override that must be preserved).
- WL-0MV6JGVPH009YDXB / WL-0MV6KV22S004NYIU / WL-0MV71WBHB007D8ZE — the mandatory always-show guarantees.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

1. **Canonical bucket order?** Priority band first (`critical` → `high` → `medium` → `low`), stage as the intra-band tie-breaker. — agreed.
2. **Does `In Review` move into its priority band?** No — it stays pinned last.
3. **Is file-path conflict grouping preserved?** Yes, within each priority band.
4. **Should selection also be priority-first before truncation?** Yes.
5. **Do labels and the core `wl next --groups` output change too?** Yes — expect `High Group N` / `Medium Group N` / `Low Group N`, with the shared copy updated in lockstep.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MM64QDA81C55S84** – Blocked issues not unblocked when blocker closed via CLI (completed)
- **WL-0MQQW534Q009JSX7** – Remove superfluous ## Stage section from wl create output (completed)
- **WL-0MSAKPVD3001JL24** – Core grouping tests for new spec (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: 0mv71wbhb007d8ze, 0mvvlbttp003y4xo, acceptance, added, already (+208 more)
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: acceptance, added, agreed, allows, already (+204 more)
- `CLI.md` — matched: 0mvvlbttp003y4xo, added, allows, already, also (+190 more)


## Plan (plan skill, 2026-11-18T23:37Z)

### Feature breakdown (test-first order)

| # | Item | Type | Depends on |
|---|------|------|------------|
| 1 | Band-order contract tests (red) — `WL-0MWMRFX27007NC0G` | task | — |
| 2 | Herdr band-first grouping — `WL-0MWMRG0BY002WEGJ` | feature | 1 |
| 3 | Core grouping mirror and CLI parity — `WL-0MWMRG3HL007PDZ6` | feature | 2 |
| 4 | Priority-first selection truncation — `WL-0MWMRG6LX006B8YO` | feature | 1 |
| 5 | Blocker-pin and substitution regression guard — `WL-0MWMRG9GQ000P52S` | task | 2, 3, 4 |
| 6 | Grouping docs and end-to-end verification — `WL-0MWMRGC32001ZJ2G` | docs | 2, 3, 4 |

### Vertical slices

- **Phase 1 (items 1-2)** — red contract tests, then the herdr grouping implementation plus its module-header documentation: an end-to-end slice through tests, code and docs for the herdr sprint-view render path.
- **Phase 2 (items 3-4)** — the core `wl next --groups` mirror with the cross-copy parity test and `CLI.md`, then the selection-truncation slice (code, tests, header docs). Items 3 and 4 are independent and may run in parallel once item 1 has landed.
- **Phase 3 (items 5-6)** — cross-cutting regression guard for blocker pinning / root substitution, then the documentation sweep and end-to-end verification.

Between phases: re-read the next item's description against what actually landed and update it before starting.

### Assumptions

- **A1** — Within a band the existing section types are kept and band-prefixed: `<Band> Group N` (file-path partitioned, covering actively-worked / `plan_complete` / `intake_complete`), a single `<Band> Idea` group and a single `<Band> Other` group; `critical` keeps `Critical Group N`. `In Review` stays one global last section. Basis: the ACs "Section order is `critical` → `high` → `medium` → `low` → `In Review`" plus "the 3-file-path-group cap applies per band-section".
- **A2** — The brief's stage sub-order (`in-progress` → `plan_complete` → `intake_complete` → `idea` → other) needs `idea: 3` and `REMAINING_STAGE_ORDER = 4` in the shared stage-order table; today `idea` and "other" share one value.
- **A3** — `others` arrive from `wl next` in score order, so a **stable** priority sort is the correct tie-break implementation; `computeScore` (`packages/shared/src/database/sort.ts`) is untouched.
- **A4** — Group labels are display-only; nothing parses them (verified: `src/commands/next.ts:247` and `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts:2577` render `groupLabel` verbatim).
- **A5** — Both grouping copies stay hand-synchronised (no shared module, per the brief); a cross-copy parity test is added as the consistency gate for the "identical order / stay in sync" AC.

### Open questions (non-blocking)

A1 was chosen because the brief says labels extend "with each band's stage sub-sections" while only `In Review` is required to remain a single global section. Re-labelling is a one-line change per copy if the producer prefers the alternative.

## Appendix: plan session (2026-11-18T23:37Z)

No new clarifying questions were put to the producer this session: the intake Appendix above (Q1-Q5) already settles the ordering, `In Review` pin, file-path grouping, selection and label questions. Two points were resolved by inspection instead of by asking:

- **Q6 — per-band `Idea` / `Other` labels.** Recorded above as a non-blocking **OPEN QUESTION** for the producer at review of `WL-0MWMRG0BY002WEGJ`; assumption A1 is the working answer.
