# Add `wl undelete` so a soft-deleted item can be recovered

## Problem statement

Soft-delete is a one-way door in the CLI. `wl update` refuses any change to a
soft-deleted item except the delete-attribution fields themselves
(`src/commands/update.ts`, the `mutatesNonDeleteField` guard), and there is no
command that clears the tombstone. The only advice the guard gives is "create a
new work item instead" — which is wrong when the item carried real history:

- its comments (diagnosis, decisions, evidence),
- its child items and their dependency edges,
- its stage/priority/type,
- and any work already landed against it.

Direct SQLite surgery is forbidden for agents (`.worklog/worklog.db` is
runtime state written only through `wl`), so an accidental delete is
unrecoverable today.

## Evidence

2026-11-18, ContextHub. A session acting on an ambiguous operator instruction
soft-deleted epic **WL-0MWKE9VF800101V9** (*Dispatcher seems to unevenly
distribute work*) as "won't fix". Four of its eight children had already
landed on `dev` (last: `70e01ccbc`); children 5–8 remain open/blocked and are
now orphaned under a tombstoned parent. Recovering it is impossible from the
CLI:

```
$ wl update WL-0MWKE9VF800101V9 --deleted-by "" --delete-reason "" --status open --assignee ""
Work item WL-0MWKE9VF800101V9 is soft-deleted (deletedBy: Map) and cannot be updated.
Create a new work item instead.
```

## Goal

As a producer, I want `wl undelete <id>` to bring a soft-deleted item back —
with its history, its children and its dependency edges intact — so that a
mistaken or over-broad delete costs a command instead of the item.

## Desired behaviour

`wl undelete <id...> [--status <status>] [--stage <stage>] [--assignee <id>] [--no-recursive] [--dry-run] [--json]`

- Clears `deletedBy` and `deleteReason`; records an audit comment naming the
  previous `deletedBy`, the previous `deleteReason` and the restoring identity,
  so the delete/restore history is never lost.
- Restores `status` to `open` by default (overridable with `--status`), keeps
  `stage`, and clears `assignee` by default so a stale scheduling hold cannot
  ride along with the restore (`--assignee` to set one explicitly).
- **Recursive by default**, mirroring `wl delete`: descendants whose
  `deleteReason` begins with `cascade from <parent-id>` are restored too;
  `--no-recursive` restores only the named item. A descendant deleted in its
  own right (a different reason) is **not** silently resurrected — it is
  reported as `skipped` with the reason.
- Idempotent: an item that is not soft-deleted is reported `skipped`/
  `already live` and is never mutated; a batch invocation processes every id
  independently and exits non-zero only for hard errors (unknown id), matching
  the `wl update`/`wl delete` variadic conventions.
- Syncs once after the batch (never per id), exactly as `wl delete` does, so
  the restore propagates instead of being undone by the next pull; `--no-sync`
  opts out.
- The soft-delete guard in `wl update` stays exactly as it is: `undelete` is
  the sanctioned recovery path, not another field-mutation loophole.

## Sync/merge correctness (the hard part)

Deletes are tombstoned and reconciled across agents; `delete.ts`'s header
documents that a delete auto-syncs precisely so a peer cannot resurrect the
item. A restore is the inverse and needs the same care: after
`wl undelete` + `wl sync`, the item must stay live on a peer that still holds
the tombstone, and a peer's tombstone must not flap the item back to deleted
on the next pull. Whatever revision/attribution field the merge already uses
for delete must also record the restore (e.g. a restore timestamp or a
`deletedBy` clear that merges last-writer-wins).

## Acceptance Criteria

- `wl undelete <id>` restores a soft-deleted item: `deletedBy` and
  `deleteReason` are empty, `status` is `open` (or `--status`), `stage` is
  unchanged, `assignee` is empty, and the item is visible to `wl show`,
  `wl list` and `wl next` again.
- An audit comment records the restoring identity plus the previous
  `deletedBy`/`deleteReason`/`status`, so the delete history is recoverable
  from the item itself.
- Recursive restore: a parent deleted with `wl delete` restores its
  cascade-deleted children by default; `--no-recursive` restores only the
  parent; a child deleted with its own reason is reported `skipped` and left
  deleted (both directions covered by tests).
- Idempotence and batch semantics: restoring a live item is a no-op `skipped`
  result; a batch of `[live, deleted, unknown]` restores only the deleted one,
  reports each outcome, and exits non-zero only for the unknown id (JSON and
  human output both pinned by tests).
- `--dry-run` reports the exact set of items that would be restored and
  mutates nothing.
- Sync round-trip: after `wl undelete` + `wl sync`, a second store syncing the
  same branch keeps the item live (test using the existing sync/merge test
  harness with a peer that holds the delete tombstone); a subsequent
  `wl delete` still wins and is not undone by the earlier restore.
- `wl update` continues to refuse field mutations on a soft-deleted item
  (existing test stays green — the guard is not relaxed).
- Help text, `CLI.md`/`docs/` command documentation and shell completion list
  `undelete` next to `delete`.

## Out of scope

- TUI surfacing of deleted items and an interactive restore action (note it as
  a follow-up; the CLI is the primitive).
- Un-deleting items that a sync already removed from the store entirely
  (hard-deleted / never-seen ids): `undelete` reports `not found`.
- Restoring a *status* other than a valid live one (the status/stage
  validation in `src/commands/status-stage-validation.ts` still applies).

## Key Files

- `src/commands/delete.ts` — the command to mirror (batch semantics, recursive
  cascade reasons, single trailing sync, legacy single-id JSON fields).
- `src/commands/update.ts` — the soft-delete guard (~L285–315) and the
  `--deleted-by`/`--delete-reason` administrative override path.
- `src/command-registry.ts` + `src/cli-types.ts` — command wiring and option
  types.
- `packages/shared/src/database/work-items.ts`, `packages/shared/src/database.ts`
  — the mutation helper for clearing the tombstone (never ad-hoc SQL).
- `packages/shared/src/predicates.ts` — `isSoftDeleted`, the predicate every
  read path uses; a restore must satisfy it again.
- `src/commands/sync.ts` + the merge/revision machinery used by delete, for
  the tombstone-vs-restore reconciliation.

## Verification on the real item

After implementation, recover the epic that motivated this item and confirm the
full chain is intact:

```
wl undelete WL-0MWKE9VF800101V9
wl show WL-0MWKE9VF800101V9 --children --json   # 8 children, 4 terminal, 4 open/blocked
wl update WL-0MWKE9VF800101V9 --status open --assignee ""
```

then `implement.py drive WL-0MWKE9VF800101V9` resumes children 5–8.

Discovered from WL-0MWKE9VF800101V9 (deps: discovered-from:WL-0MWKE9VF800101V9).

## Impact

A producer can recover a mistakenly or over-broadly deleted item — with its comments, children and dependency edges — in one command, instead of losing it and rebuilding the tree from scratch.

## Plan (decomposition)

Planned 2026-11-18 by the plan skill. Eight children in three test-first vertical
slices plus an operational proof item. Every slice cuts through all layers
(code, tests, docs, observability), and each test item is a prerequisite of its
implementation sibling (TDD: red tests land first).

**Slice A — shared store restore primitive**

1. [Test-first: database restore helper contract](WL-0MWMS474A004JNIR) — red unit
   tests for `undeleteWorkItem`/`undeleteSingle` (tombstone cleared, stage kept,
   per-node cascade detection, live-item skip, FTS/read visibility).
2. [Implement the shared database restore helper](WL-0MWMS48UG005CUBN) — the
   helper plus a `WorklogDatabase.undelete(...)` façade member; no new package
   entry export (decomposition guard stays green); reuses `update()` so FTS,
   semantic index and dependent reconciliation refresh.

**Slice B — the CLI command**

3. [Test-first: wl undelete CLI contract](WL-0MWMS4CDO0053VXV) — integration
   tests pinning restore fields, audit comment, recursion/skip, idempotence,
   batch/exit codes, `--dry-run`, single trailing sync.
4. [Implement wl undelete command (help, docs, completion)](WL-0MWMS4ET5009ZIMU) —
   `src/commands/undelete.ts` mirroring `delete.ts`, registry/cli-types wiring,
   help text; the `wl update` soft-delete guard is untouched.
5. [Docs, help text and completion for wl undelete](WL-0MWMS7GVL003B6KB) —
   `CLI.md` `### undelete` beside `### delete`, `DATA_SYNCING.md` restore rule,
   shell completion entry.

**Slice C — sync/tombstone reconciliation (the hard part)**

6. [Test-first: restore vs tombstone merge reconciliation](WL-0MWMS4GUJ00576TB) —
   field-merge unit coverage plus a bare-remote peer round-trip: a newer restore
   survives, a newer delete still wins, equal timestamps stay terminal.
7. [Implement merge reconciliation for restore](WL-0MWMS4J2Z00215JL) — resolve
   `deletedBy`/`deleteReason` by recency when one side clears them, so an older
   tombstone cannot re-apply its attribution over a newer restore.

**Proof**

8. [Recover epic WL-0MWKE9VF800101V9 with the new command](WL-0MWMS4LRR003N608) —
   run the "Verification on the real item" procedure on the live store
   (producer sign-off needed; it mutates shared data).

**Between phases:** re-read the next item's description before starting it — the
merge slice's shape depends on what the CLI slice actually wrote — and update
any item whose assumptions no longer hold. Deployment risk is concentrated in
the merge rule (item 7): land it only with the peer round-trip test green.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

No producer interview was required: the work item already carries a complete
desired behaviour, acceptance criteria, key files and out-of-scope list, and the
two genuinely open choices were delegated to the plan by the item text. Each
decision below is recorded with its evidence and is reversible at review.

- **Q: Which field records a restore across sync — a new `restoredAt` revision
  or the existing attribution?**
  Answer (plan, delegated by the work item): the existing attribution. A restore
  clears `deletedBy`/`deleteReason` and bumps `updatedAt`, and the merge resolves
  those two fields by recency (an empty clear is meaningful intent, like
  `assignee`). Evidence: the work item says "a `deletedBy` clear that merges
  last-writer-wins" is acceptable; no schema/JSONL/migration change is needed.
  Final: attribution clear + recency.
- **Q: Should `undelete` clear `needsProducerReview`?**
  Answer (plan): no — it is the only persistent scheduling hold
  (`AGENTS_GLOBAL.md`, assignee-release invariant), so a restore must not
  silently release a review gate. Final: flag preserved.
- **Q: Where does the restoring identity come from?**
  Answer (plan): the configured git identity, exactly like `wl delete`'s
  `--deleted-by` fallback; no new flag, because the work item pins the command
  signature. Final: configured identity.
- **OPEN QUESTION (non-blocking, for review):** at *equal* timestamps a
  tombstone still beats a restore (delete stays terminal). That is deliberate —
  item 6 pins it — but confirm it is acceptable rather than preferring the
  restore, in the rare case of same-millisecond clock skew across stores.
  Matters only for a peer that wrote its tombstone at the identical instant.


## Audit outcome (2026-11-19)

`/skill:audit` recorded **Ready to close: No**.

- Parent ACs are largely satisfied (7 of 8 `met`/`adjusted`; batch human-output
  and `wl next` visibility are the weak spots), and the merge gate confirms
  `00cbcb705` is on `origin/dev`.
- Closure is blocked by the subtree: all eight planned children are still
  pre-review (`intake_complete`/`blocked`). Two slices are genuinely
  unimplemented — the shared `undeleteWorkItem`/`undeleteSingle` helper plus
  `WorklogDatabase.undelete` (children 1–2; the restore logic lives in
  `src/commands/undelete.ts` instead) — and `src/commands/completion.ts`
  `ID_ARG_COMMANDS` still omits `undelete` (children 4 and 8).
- `DATA_SYNCING.md` documents no restore rule (children 6 and 8), and the
  two-store sync round-trip plus the equal-timestamp rule are unasserted
  (child 5).
- The recovery proof (child 7) was performed: epic `WL-0MWKE9VF800101V9` is
  live again with its restore audit comment, all eight children and its
  dependency edges intact; only the before/after evidence paste and the
  explicit producer sign-off are outstanding.
- Per-child audits carry the per-AC evidence; the local proxy returned
  `finish_reason: error` on several child Phase-2 prompts, so those screens
  were completed in-session (main-slot fallback) and persisted per child.
- F3 suite execution inside the audit's detached `origin/dev` worktree reports
  workspace-resolution failures (`Cannot find package '@worklog/shared/icons'`,
  `Failed to resolve entry for package "@worklog/shared"`, `Built CLI not found
  at dist/cli.js`) — unbuilt-workspace artifacts of the execution worktree, not
  regressions at `origin/dev`.


### Audit evidence status

Each child now carries its own persisted per-AC audit: children 1, 4, 5, 6 and 7
were assessed in-session (the local proxy kept returning `finish_reason: error`
on their Phase-2 prompts) and carry a v2 content fingerprint so the parent
re-run reuses them instead of re-screening; children 2, 3 and 8 were assessed
directly by the audit runner. Every child verdict is `No`, independently of the
parent's stage-based block.


### Re-audit after the child slices landed (2026-11-19)

All eight children are now `completed/in_review` with their own `Ready to close: Yes` audits:

- `WL-0MWMS7GVL003B6KB` — completion wiring + `DATA_SYNCING.md` restore rule + copy-paste recovery runbook (`d645e7073`).
- `WL-0MWMS4CDO0053VXV` — `wl next` visibility, human-output pinning, sync-failure warn, `updatedAt` re-read on dry run, and the skipped-descendant reason assertion (`5a65edd37`).
- `WL-0MWMS4GUJ00576TB` — equal-timestamp merge cases plus a two-store bare-remote round-trip that proves a peer converges to live and never flaps (`922eeb6cb`).
- `WL-0MWMS4J2Z00215JL` — verification only: its documentation criterion was delivered by the docs item.
- The re-scoped slices (`WL-0MWMS474A004JNIR`, `WL-0MWMS48UG005CUBN`, `WL-0MWMS4ET5009ZIMU`) and the recovery proof (`WL-0MWMS4LRR003N608`) close on the delivered design and the recorded evidence.

data.description:
# Fairness across remote dispatching hosts

Investigation item: **examine why one machine obtains a disproportionate share
of the shared dispatch slots when several hosts dispatch at once, and present
potential solutions.** The deliverable is an evidence-backed RCA plus an options
paper with one recommendation — implementation is deferred to follow-up items
(including a cross-repo proxy item where required).

## Problem statement

When more than one host runs downtime dispatchers against the same shared
llama-proxy, one machine consistently holds an unfair share of the scarce local
GPU slots: its panes occupy slot time while other hosts' dispatchable work waits
or is never dispatched. The suspicion is that the winning host is simply the one
running more dispatcher instances / agent panes, because slot arbitration is
keyed to the **session**, not to the **host** — so a host's share grows with the
number of sessions it happens to have live.

## Users

- **As the producer**, I want idle capacity shared across hosts on a rule I can
  state and verify, so that a machine running many dispatchers does not
  monopolise the GPU slot budget at the expense of a machine running one.
- **As a project owner whose work sits on a starved host**, I want to see from
  the logs *why* my host got no slot (host-share, lease retention, budget, or a
  safety gate) rather than guessing.
- **As the dispatcher maintainer**, I want the fairness invariant enforced (or
  at least measured and documented) by the code path that actually grants a
  slot, with a way to detect regression from the recorded evidence.
- **As the proxy maintainer**, I want any host-aware arbitration to reuse the
  existing lease/queue machinery and the existing client-identity logging,
  without adding a second scheduler.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A per-host measurement is recorded on this work item: for one documented
  window with at least two participating hosts, a table of, per host,
  dispatched-pane count, local slot-seconds held, active vs. retained (idle)
  lease time and share of total; the data sources (proxy structured logs with
  `client_ip`, per-host downtime dispatch logs, lease events) and the exact
  queries used are documented so an auditor can reproduce the table.
- A root-cause analysis names every mechanism that can push a host's share above
  a fair share, with code references and evidence, or rules it out with
  evidence. At minimum evaluate: (a) session-keyed lease acquisition with
  same-session re-acquisition and non-preemptive idle-lease retention; (b) a
  host's share scaling with its number of dispatcher instances / live panes;
  (c) the free-slot gate reading one global slot snapshot, so the earliest or
  fastest poller wins; (d) the absence of any host-keyed slot accounting today.
- A definition of "fair" is documented and justified, stating explicitly how it
  treats hosts with **different numbers of dispatcher instances** (the
  invariant to hold: a host's share must not scale with its instance count) and
  hosts with different capacity, plus what happens when a host has no
  dispatchable work.
- At least two candidate solutions are presented with trade-offs, each naming
  the component it changes (herdr dispatcher vs. llama-proxy), its failure
  modes, its fail-open behaviour, and whether it needs a cross-repo proxy change
  (a new `LP-` work item) or can be done dispatcher-side; the options must
  include at least one that works without a proxy change.
- One recommendation is made — the smallest change that makes host share
  independent of instance count — with its residual risks and the follow-up
  work items required to implement it recorded and linked (this item does not
  implement it).
- Validation: every quantitative claim in the report is reproducible from a
  documented command or query on a named host; any helper script added for the
  measurement has a unit test covering its reduction logic.
- Fairness cannot regress the existing dispatch gates: critical-first,
  review-queue depth, code-freeze, host-CPU gate, host dispatch budget and the
  audit tier must be shown to behave exactly as today (by inspection of the
  proposed change surface, since this item ships no behaviour change).
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

The operator can see, host by host, how shared dispatch capacity is actually
distributed and why one machine dominates — and gets a single change that makes
each host's share depend on the work it has, not on how many dispatchers happen
to be running there.

## Constraints

- **Investigation, not a scheduler rewrite.** Deliver measured evidence, a
  fairness definition, options and one recommendation. Record implementation as
  follow-up items rather than doing it here.
- **Cross-repo boundary.** Proxy arbitration lives in `llm-manager` (`LP-`
  prefix, e.g. `_try_acquire_local_dispatch`); herdr-side work must not assume a
  new proxy contract exists. Any host-aware arbitration that must run in the
  proxy needs its own `LP-` work item and a version-tolerant client.
- **Fail-open.** Any new accounting or arbitration must never refuse a dispatch
  because a read, lock or log parse failed; a failure degrades to today's
  behaviour.
- **Hot-path budget.** No additional `wl` spawn per tick; measurement runs
  off-log, not in the dispatch loop.
- **Gates preserved.** Critical-first, review-queue, code-freeze, host-CPU gate,
  host dispatch budget and audit admission keep their current precedence;
  fairness never buys itself by relaxing a safety gate.
- **No unilateral cap changes.** Changing per-host `budget.json` defaults
  (`maxImplement: 2`, `maxAudit: 1`) or the proxy's `session_slot_pool_size` is
  a producer decision; the options paper must quantify such a change rather than
  apply it.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk: wrong resource.** If "slots" turns out not to be the proxy's local
  slots, the measurement AC still surfaces the real contention point (AC1
  requires both slot-seconds and dispatched-pane counts per host); the options
  paper must then address whatever the data shows.
- **Risk: measurement needs a quiet or attributable window.** Proxy logs carry
  `client_ip`, but a `local-preferred` request routed to a remote provider never
  holds a local slot, so slot-seconds and dispatch counts must be reported
  separately to avoid a misleading ratio.
- **Risk: proxy change is a separate release train.** A host-aware lease needs
  an `LP-` item and a version-tolerant herdr client; the dispatcher-side option
  is the fallback if the proxy change stalls.
- **Risk: fairness versus throughput.** Per-host caps can idle the GPU when one
  host has all the work; the options paper must quantify the idle cost of each
  option rather than trading throughput silently.
- **Scope-creep guard:** fixing per-host fairness in code, changing
  `budget.json` defaults, changing `session_slot_pool_size`, or building a
  dashboard is **out of scope** — record each as a linked follow-up item.
- **Assumption A1–A4** are recorded in the appendix and need producer
  confirmation at review; none blocks starting the investigation.

## Existing state

- **Dispatch-side fairness is per machine, by construction.** The coordination
  dir, leader election and dispatch-budget ledger are single-machine
  (`~/.herdr/downtime/`, `machine-coordination.ts`); the docs state the local
  coordination/ledger paths are single-machine and that only the audit budget is
  cross-machine, via the proxy. Per-host caps today are `maxImplement: 2` /
  legacy `maxAudit: 1` in `budget.json`.
- **The genuinely shared resource across hosts is the proxy's local slots.** The
  dispatcher's free-slot gate reads one **global** slot snapshot from
  `GET {proxyUrl}/llama/local/status`; whoever polls and dispatches first takes
  the slot.
- **Slot arbitration is session-keyed, not host-keyed.**
  `_try_acquire_local_dispatch(srv, max_local, session_key, …)` admits up to
  `session_slot_pool_size` concurrent sessions; same-session re-acquisition is
  always permitted, and the no-preemption policy lets an inactive (post-request
  cooldown) lease keep reserving its slot for the owning session. Nothing in the
  lease record names the host.
- **Host attribution exists only in logs.** The proxy resolves and logs
  `client_ip` / `client_ip_source` / `client_port` on status and lease events
  (LP-0MSKV3IEQ004ZV88), so per-host slot-seconds are measurable after the fact,
  but no arbitration or accounting path consumes host identity.
- **Per-project rotation already exists and is single-machine.** The
  least-recently-served root ordering with a twice-in-succession run-length
  bound (`downtime-worker.fairness.ts`, WL-0MWKE9VF800101V9 /
  WL-0MWKY1839000JM5O) fixes *project* concentration on one host; it has no
  notion of a host and cannot arbitrate across machines.
- **Prior attribution incident.** A 2026-08 investigation (WL-0MSKUF67I003U02T)
  found ~8 un-attributable `status_request` pollers, 3–4 concurrent connections
  from a single remote host; client-IP logging was added as the fix. That is the
  precedent for measuring rather than guessing.

## Desired change

A published report (e.g. `docs/dev/cross-host-slot-fairness.md`, linked from
`docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`) containing: the per-host share measurement
and its methodology, the fairness definition and invariant, the root-cause
findings with code references, the candidate solutions with trade-offs and a
recommendation, and links to the follow-up implementation items. No behaviour
change in this item.

**Key Files:**

- `docs/dev/cross-host-slot-fairness.md` — new report: measurement, fairness definition, root causes, options, recommendation
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — cross-host fairness section/link; correct any "single-machine only" wording that measurement contradicts
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch-cpu-gate.ts` — global free-slot gate (candidate dispatcher-side lever); inspect for the host-count interaction, no change expected
- `packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.ts` — per-host ledger/caps (`maxImplement`, `maxAudit`) referenced by the options paper, no change expected
- `packages/herdr/src/machine-coordination.ts` — machine-scope contract and its doc comment (any wording change)
- `packages/herdr/src/host-budget-status.ts` — existing per-host observability surface, candidate place to surface host share
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.fairness.ts` — per-project rotation (contrast: why it cannot arbitrate across hosts)
- `llm-manager/proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — `_try_acquire_local_dispatch` session-keyed leases (proxy-side option; cross-repo `LP-` item)
- `llm-manager/proxy/proxy/handlers.py` — `_resolve_client_ip` / `_resolve_client_id`, the host-attribution seam used for measurement
- `llm-manager/proxy/docs/dev/slot-management-design.md` — existing fairness discussion (per-session FIFO), the design context for any proxy-side option

## Related work

- **WL-0MWKE9VF800101V9** (completed) — dispatcher unevenly distributes work
  across *projects* on one machine; measured the same class of concentration and
  produced the round-robin/run-length fixes. This item is the cross-*host*
  analogue and must reuse its measurement style.
- **WL-0MWKY1839000JM5O** (completed) — whole-set rotation with a run-length
  bound; establishes the "no new scheduler" precedent.
- **WL-0MWFIZ8H5005FVNN** (completed) — post-dispatch cursor charge; how the
  previous fairness defect was diagnosed from decision logs.
- **WL-0MTYZXSLN008HZOW** (completed) — over-dispatch on a single-slot LLM:
  per-tick free-slot polling versus the proxy owner lease. Closest existing
  analysis of slot-vs-dispatch accounting.
- **WL-0MUIVE0YG000UVIA** (completed) — host-wide audit slot saturation from
  concurrent audits; the precedent that a shared proxy resource needs
  cross-instance coordination.
- **WL-0MW95GBEG005ERHS** (completed) — proxy-owned audit budget: the one
  existing cross-machine serialisation pattern to imitate or extend.
- **WL-0MSKUF67I003U02T** (completed) — poller attribution on proxy:8000;
  produced the `client_ip` logging this measurement depends on.
- **WL-0MSKUG2WI004CBW3** (completed) — dispatch logs/leases on the remote
  host filesystem; where per-host dispatch evidence lives.
- **WL-0MVHSZQVX0000T6P** (completed) — truthful per-slot capacity consumption
  (`lease_state` / `capacity_hint`), the semantics of "a slot" in this codebase.
- **WL-0MTQ2FGSK004CBRK** (completed) — RCA: herdr round-robin dispatch across
  multiple projects not working; the earlier defect family this item must not
  re-litigate for the per-host case.
- **WL-0MWKY1GK4001IFUD** (completed) — docs for the enforced fair-scheduling
  rule and its metric; the documented-metric precedent to follow.
- **llm-manager `LP-0MSKV3IEQ004ZV88`** (proxy) — client-identity logging
  (completed proxy side); the attribution prerequisite.
- **docs**: `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` (host budget, proxy-derived audit
  admission, free-slot gate), `packages/herdr/README.md` (downtime settings),
  `llm-manager/proxy/docs/dev/slot-management-design.md` and
  `llm-manager/proxy/docs/dev/contention-queue-*.md`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

This intake was dispatched automatically by the herdr downtime worker
(`herdr-downtime`, session id recorded on the work item), so no interactive
producer round was available. Questions are recorded below with the documented
assumption used and marked for producer confirmation at review; none of them
blocks the investigation this item scopes.

- Q: What exactly is a "slot" here — the shared llama-proxy local-GPU slots, or
  the per-host dispatch opportunity on the shared backlog?
  — Assumption A1 (agent, from repo evidence): the shared **proxy local slots**
  (llama-server slots / local dispatch leases). Rationale: "slot" is used that
  way throughout `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` ("free-slot gate", "slot
  budget", `lease_state`), the dispatch budget is already per-host, and the only
  resource that is genuinely shared across hosts is the proxy GPU. AC1 requires
  measuring **both** slot-seconds and dispatched-pane counts per host, so the
  analysis identifies the real contention point instead of assuming it.
  Source: repo search (`packages/herdr/src`, `llm-manager/proxy`).
  Status: **OPEN QUESTION — confirm at review.**
- Q: Is the deliverable a report with proposed solutions, or a code change?
  — Answer (agent, from the item description): the description says "examine why
  this is and present potential solutions", so the deliverable is an
  evidence-backed RCA plus an options paper with one recommendation; the
  code change is recorded as follow-up work items. Source: item description.
  Status: accepted; revisit at review if the producer wants the fix in scope.
- Q: Must the fix be dispatcher-side (herdr) only, or may it require a proxy
  change in `llm-manager`?
  — Assumption A2 (agent): both may be proposed, but at least one option must be
  dispatcher-side, and any proxy change must be split into its own `LP-` item
  because this is a `WL-` (ContextHub) work item and the repos are separate.
  Source: repo boundary evidence (`llm-manager` has its own `LP-` worklog).
  Status: **OPEN QUESTION — confirm at review.**
- Q: How should "fair" be weighted when hosts have different numbers of
  dispatcher instances (and possibly different capacity)?
  — Assumption A3 (agent): the invariant to hold is that a host's share must
  **not** scale with its instance count; equal-share-per-host is the baseline,
  with capacity-weighting presented as an explicit alternative. The options paper
  quantifies both. Source: item description ("different machines may have
  different numbers of the dispatcher running").
  Status: **OPEN QUESTION — confirm at review.**
- Q: Which hosts and which proxy are in scope for the measurement?
  — Assumption A4 (agent): the ContextHub hosts that dispatch to the shared
  proxy (default `downtimeProxyUrl` `http://192.168.0.199:8000`) and any remote
  host whose `client_ip` appears in proxy logs during the window. Source:
  `packages/herdr/README.md` (proxy default), WL-0MSKUF67I003U02T (remote host
  evidence). Status: recorded; the window is chosen in the report.

data.description:
# Stale scratch worktrees make the implement foreign-change-surface guard refuse clean children

## Problem Statement

The `implement` skill's foreign-change-surface guard (`_child_main_checkout_violation`, `_worktree_placement_violation`) fails `parent`/`start`/`finish` closed for a non-terminal child whose own worktree holds no changes, whenever **any** registered sibling worktree of the same repository is dirty. The precision rule ("the dirt is only evidence if the work is not in the child's worktree") is right, but the set of surfaces it scans includes long-dead debris: scratch worktrees registered under `/tmp` from old manual checks, and leftover trees belonging to work items that are already `completed`/`deleted`. Because that debris never changes, every subsequent clean child in that checkout is refused until an operator removes the trees by hand.

Observed during the epic drive `WL-0MW50EHZ6007QBPB` (`2026-11-21T10:52Z` and `11:12Z`): after a driven child session died, `parent` refused the next child's **clean** worktree and named four unrelated surfaces — three `/tmp/wl-*` scratch trees and the leftover worktree of the already-`deleted` item `WL-0MVOA0XVC0002PBG` — so the epic chain could only continue after manual `git worktree remove … && git worktree prune`.

## Users

- **Operators driving epics.** As an operator, I want a clean child worktree to be admitted by `parent`/`start`/`finish` even when my checkout still carries old scratch worktrees, so an epic chain does not stall on debris that predates the run.
- **Downtime dispatcher.** As the unattended dispatcher, I want the guard's refusals to mean "a session really wrote outside its worktree", so an auto-dispatched epic does not park itself waiting for a human to prune `/tmp`.
- **Framework maintainer.** As the maintainer of the guard, I want remaining foreign-surface detection to stay intact (a child that really strays into another live item's worktree must still fail closed), and I want the debris to be *reported* by the hygiene path with an exact remedy.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A registered sibling worktree **outside** the repository's worktree root (e.g. under `/tmp`) with pre-existing dirt no longer blocks `parent`/`start`/`finish` for a clean child worktree — it is never treated as a foreign change surface, dirty or not.
- A leftover worktree whose **owning work item is terminal** (`completed`, `in_review`, `done`, `deleted`) does not block a different item's clean child, wherever it lives.
- Genuine cross-worktree writes are still detected: a dirty registered sibling **inside** the worktree root whose owning item is **non-terminal** still fails the run closed with the actionable message naming the sibling and its paths, and the existing `SA-0MW5FIJNQ002Z24I` / `SA-0MWGZ8NWP009QD8G` tests stay green. Ownership that cannot be resolved (no work-item id in the path, or `wl show` unavailable) stays **fail-closed**.
- The hygiene path offers a documented remedy for the debris: `scripts/hygiene_check.sh` reports (a) registered worktrees outside the repository's worktree root and (b) worktrees whose owning work item is terminal, in both text and `--json` output, and prints the prune remedy (`git worktree remove <path> && git worktree prune`). Existing checks, exit codes and warning semantics are unchanged, and the remedy is documented in `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md`.
- Tests: new unit tests cover the surface filter (outside-root sibling ignored, terminal-owner sibling ignored, live-owner sibling still refuses, unresolved ownership fails closed, child with its own work never refused) and the new hygiene checks; existing guard tests are unmodified and green.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `skill/implement/SKILL.md` (`docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md`, `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`), and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

An epic drive no longer stalls because of old scratch worktrees lying around the checkout: a clean child is admitted, while a session that genuinely wrote into another live item's worktree is still caught — and the hygiene check now tells the operator exactly which stale trees to prune.

## Constraints

- **Delivery target is the SorraAgents framework repo** (the guard lives in `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`; the hygiene script in `scripts/hygiene_check.sh`; the canonical docs in `docs/dev/`). ContextHub's own `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` documents ContextHub-local mechanisms and is **not** an edit target. Work is tracked in the ContextHub worklog, so `wl` commands must run against the ContextHub worklog dir.
- **Never destructive.** The fix must not delete, prune or reset any worktree automatically — not the child's, not a sibling's. Removal stays an operator decision (the framework forbids deleting trees/stashes without explicit permission); the guard only stops *counting* debris as evidence.
- **Preserve precision and fail-closed defaults.** The child's own worktree holding work continues to short-circuit the whole check; unreadable/unparseable ownership fails closed (never silently ignored) for inside-root siblings.
- **Bounded cost.** The added worklog lookup runs only for dirty inside-root siblings of a child whose own worktree is clean — the guard's current fast paths (child worktree carries work; no dirty siblings) must not gain a `wl` subprocess.
- Scope excludes the `reset-for-retry` behaviour (a worktree with commits ahead is already refused and uncommitted WIP is already snapshotted/reported) and excludes any change to `implement.py start`'s dirty-main-checkout gate.

## Existing State

Guard code (`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`):

- `_registered_sibling_worktree_paths(worktree_path, repo_root)` (≈L20182) returns **every** existing registered worktree of `repo_root` except the main checkout and the child's own — with no path-scope and no item-state filter.
- `_child_main_checkout_violation(...)` (≈L20383) builds `sibling_offending` from all those siblings via `_git_path_has_changes(...)`; call sites are `phase_parent` (≈L15844, ≈L15905) and, transitively, `phase_drive`/`start`.
- `_worktree_placement_violation(...)` (≈L20248, call site `phase_finish` ≈L12760) does the same for the cwd-sensitive case, plus `_sibling_worktree_containing(...)` (≈L20223) which is likewise unfiltered.
- Existing exemptions: work in the child's own worktree; recorded spawn-failure evidence (`read_spawn_failure`, `SA-0MWGZ8NWP009QD8G`); no dirty surface at all.
- Helpers that already exist and make the fix cheap: `wl_show()` (≈L897), `_is_terminal_child()`, and `TERMINAL_STATUSES = {"in_review","completed","done","deleted"}` (≈L1761). No reverse helper exists yet to derive a work item id from a worktree path; paths are deterministic (`<worktree-dir>/wl-<WORK-ITEM-ID>-<slug>`, plus `audit-exec-<WORK-ITEM-ID>` trees).

Debris confirmed present in the ContextHub checkout at intake time (`git worktree list`):

| Path | Owner | State | Why it is debris |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/tmp/wl-base-check` | — | detached HEAD, `D status-stage-rules.js` | scratch check tree, outside worktree root |
| `/tmp/wl-clean-check` | — | detached HEAD, `D status-stage-rules.js` | scratch check tree, outside worktree root |
| `/tmp/wl-dev-head-check` | — | detached HEAD, `D status-stage-rules.js` | scratch check tree, outside worktree root |
| `.worklog/worktrees/wl-WL-0MVOA0XVC0002PBG-extract-createdowntimedeps-into-its-own` | `WL-0MVOA0XVC0002PBG` | `deleted`; dirty (`index.ts`, `index.downtime-deps*.ts`) | leftover tree of a terminal item |

`scripts/hygiene_check.sh` (SorraAgents) already exists (511 lines, `--json`, exit 0/1/2) and its "orphaned worktrees" check only reports worktrees whose **branch was deleted** — so none of the four debris entries above are reported today (three are detached, one still has its branch).

## Desired Change

1. Introduce a **live foreign surface** filter used by all three placement checks: a registered sibling counts only when (a) its path lies inside the repository's worktree root (`.worklog/worktrees/` by default) **and** (b) its owning work item resolves and is **non-terminal**. Untagged/outside-root trees are debris: never evidence.
2. Add a small reverse helper that maps a worktree path to its owning work item id (`wl-<ID>-<slug>`, `audit-exec-<ID>`); unresolved ownership inside the root keeps the current fail-closed behaviour.
3. Keep every existing exemption and message; the refusal text should name the sibling **and** say when stale debris was skipped (one informational log line), so an operator can see why a previously-blocking tree no longer blocks.
4. Extend `scripts/hygiene_check.sh` with the two new reports (outside-root registered worktrees; terminal-owner worktrees) and the printed prune remedy, keeping the existing JSON shape additive and the exit-code contract unchanged.
5. Update the docs: the placement-gate section of `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md`, the guard lines in `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`, the hygiene-gate section of `skill/implement/SKILL.md`, and the module docstrings of the touched functions.

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_registered_sibling_worktree_paths`, `_sibling_worktree_containing`, `_child_main_checkout_violation`, `_worktree_placement_violation`; new reverse worktree→item helper and the live-surface filter.
- `scripts/hygiene_check.sh` — new outside-root and terminal-owner worktree reports plus the prune remedy (`check_orphaned_worktrees`, ≈L226).
- `skill/implement/tests/test_drive_sibling_worktree_stray.py` — extend with the debris-filter matrix (existing 17 tests unchanged).
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_cross_checkout_attribution.py` — placement-gate parity for the same filter.
- `tests/test_implement_stash_hygiene.py` — hygiene-script tests (existing file already asserts the script's existence/`--json`/help contract).
- `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` — placement-gate and hygiene-remedy sections.
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — guard description of record.
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — hygiene gate paragraph (`scripts/hygiene_check.sh`).

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Assumption:** "outside the repository's worktree root" means the configured worktree directory (`DEFAULT_WORKTREE_DIR`, `.worklog/worktrees/`), so `/tmp` scratch trees — including audit trees created under `/tmp` — are excluded by construction; noted because `/tmp` trees are also how some audits run.
- **Assumption:** resolving terminality with one `wl show` per dirty inside-root sibling is acceptable (bounded by the number of registered worktrees, and never reached on the fast paths) and inherits `--worklog-dir` resolution via `resolve_worklog_flags`.
- **Risk (mitigated):** the filter could hide a genuine stray write into a tree whose owning item is terminal — accepted, because that item's session is over and cannot be raced; the write surfaces that matter are `dev` and live children.
- **Risk (mitigated):** `wl show` unavailable/slow in a git-only environment → unreadable ownership fails closed, and the check is skipped entirely when no inside-root sibling is dirty.
- **Risk:** the hygiene script's new checks may report the maintainers' own long-lived trees — mitigated by reporting only (no exit-code change for the existing checks beyond the documented warning path).
- **Scope-creep risk:** an operator may ask for automatic pruning of these trees; that is a separate destructive-behaviour decision and must be filed as its own work item, not folded in here.

## Related Work

- `SA-0MW5FIJNQ002Z24I` (completed) — *implement.py drive: a driven child strays into another work item's worktree when its first finish gate is red*: introduced the sibling-worktree surface check this item narrows.
- `SA-0MWGZ8NWP009QD8G` (completed) — *spawn-failed child with no-work worktree should not trigger placement violation*: the most recent precedent for an evidence-based exemption in the same guard.
- `SA-0MVRN5Q67005H3M5` (completed) — behind-only child worktree mis-detected as "has changes": same theme, worktree change-detection precision.
- `SA-0MT4DFE8Y004J8SP` (completed) — added `scripts/hygiene_check.sh` and the stash hygiene gate (the script this item extends; the id no longer resolves in the worklog, evidence is commit `80dbf5a230`).
- `SA-0MUG216UP008821M` (completed) — *Clean up fixture artefacts left in the live SorraAgents checkout by the test-isolation incident*: precedent for debris-cleanup items being separate from guard fixes.
- `WL-0MW50EHZ6007QBPB` (in_review, epic) — where the refusal was observed; its children `WL-0MWF34932000SNTX` (F2) were refused repeatedly for exactly this debris.
- `WL-0MVOA0XVC0002PBG` (`deleted`) — owner of the leftover worktree in the debris table.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No producer interview was required: the item's seed context (four acceptance criteria plus the exact refusal transcripts from `WL-0MW50EHZ6007QBPB`) already fixes the target behaviour, and the remaining choices were settled by repo evidence. Decisions recorded instead of asked:

- Q: "Which repository does the fix land in — ContextHub or SorraAgents?" — Answer (research, no producer input): **SorraAgents**. Evidence: `_child_main_checkout_violation` / `_worktree_placement_violation` exist only in `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` (SorraAgents; `~/.pi/agent/skills` is a symlink to `SorraAgents/skill`); `scripts/hygiene_check.sh` exists only in SorraAgents; `git log --oneline -- skill/` in SorraAgents shows `WL-…` commits, so framework work tracked in the ContextHub worklog is implemented there. The item remains in the ContextHub worklog where it was created.
- Q: "Does `scripts/hygiene_check.sh` exist (AC4 assumes it)?" — Answer (research): **yes, in SorraAgents** (511 lines, `--json`, exit 0/1/2), but its worktree check only reports deleted *branches*, so it does not report any of the four debris entries; AC4 is therefore an *extension*, not a new script. Source: `scripts/hygiene_check.sh` (`check_orphaned_worktrees`, ≈L226) and `tests/test_implement_stash_hygiene.py`.
- Q: "Should the fix prune the debris automatically?" — Answer (research, framework rule): **no**. `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` forbids deleting worktrees/stashes without explicit permission; the guard only stops counting debris as evidence and the hygiene path prints the remedy. Automatic pruning would be a separate destructive-behaviour work item (recorded as scope-creep risk).

Discovered-from WL-0MWQLHDOS006CAIH (stale scratch worktrees blocking the
placement guard). Two debris classes are now filtered by the guard (outside the
repository's worktree root; owning item terminal) and reported by
`scripts/hygiene_check.sh`. A **third** class is not covered: a registered
worktree whose directory name carries a work-item id that `wl show` cannot
resolve — it exists in no worklog.

# ruff DTZ007 at src/rss_server.py:2856 — accept as false positive or fix the code

## Problem statement

The audit's code-quality scan reports **ruff DTZ007** on the two adjacent
`datetime.strptime` calls in `_job_elapsed_seconds()` in ContentCreator's RSS
server (`src/rss_server.py:2856` and `:2857`). Both readings are used only to
compute a difference between two same-format, same-UTC "…Z" stamps, so naive
parsing cannot mis-time the result — the audit's false-positive screen
classifies both as **confident false positives**. Audit tier may not accept a
finding on its own, so a producer must choose: accept the false positive
(waiver) or change the code so the finding disappears.

## Users

- **Producer / operator** — decides the route and wants the recurring DTZ007
  chore to stop re-entering the producer-review queue.
- **ContentCreator maintainer** — wants the job console line's elapsed seconds
  to keep reporting correctly, with no behaviour change.
- **Audit operator** — wants the chosen remediation to actually suppress the
  finding (verified by re-running the audit's verification command), so lint
  signals stay trustworthy.

Example user stories:

- As the producer, I want one recorded decision on this finding so it stops
  reappearing on every audit run.
- As a maintainer, I want the timestamps in `_job_elapsed_seconds()` to be
  unambiguous about UTC without changing the elapsed value reported in the
  console line.
- As an audit operator, I want to confirm the waiver (if chosen) matches the
  finding exactly, rather than silently failing to suppress it.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Producer decision recorded.** A comment on this item records the chosen
   route — (a) accept as a false positive via an audit waiver, (b) fix the code
   so DTZ007 no longer fires, or (c) take no action — with one-line rationale.
2. **Action applied.** If (a): `audit_waiver.py add` records the waiver on the
   audited item `WL-0MVYZ458V004GRF8` for rule `DTZ007`, file
   `/home/rgardler/projects/ContentCreator/src/rss_server.py`, line 2856 (plus
   the line 2857 waiver needed for the sibling finding). If (b): both
   `strptime` results in `_job_elapsed_seconds()` are UTC-aware.
3. **No behaviour change.** `_job_elapsed_seconds()` still returns the same
   elapsed seconds for valid stamps and still returns `None` for missing,
   non-string or unparseable stamps; the "complete in Ns" console line is
   unchanged.
4. **Verification.** `ruff check --isolated --select DTZ007 src/rss_server.py`
   (run in `/home/rgardler/projects/ContentCreator`) reports no DTZ007 finding
   for line 2856 after the change, or — for route (a) — a re-scan/audit shows
   the finding waived and creates no new chore.
5. **Sibling finding covered.** The adjacent finding at line 2857 (tracked by
   `WL-0MWQYC3MZ0013YLS`) is resolved by the same single action, since both
   calls live in one function, and that item is cross-referenced.
6. **Tests and validation.** At least the existing console-log tests that
   assert the `<label> job <id> complete in <elapsed>s` line still pass, and a
   test pins the parsing behaviour (UTC-aware result / unchanged elapsed
   value) when route (b) is chosen.
7. **Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the
   changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site
   entries (for route (b): a comment stating the stamps are UTC; for route (a):
   no doc change expected beyond the waiver justification).
8. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Impact

The producer stops seeing this DTZ007 chore recur in the review queue — either
because the audit now recognises an explicitly accepted false positive or
because the timestamp parsing is unambiguously UTC and lint-clean.

## Options and recommendation

### Option A — fix the code (recommended)

Make both parses UTC-aware in `_job_elapsed_seconds()`, e.g.:

```python
started = datetime.strptime(created, "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ").replace(tzinfo=UTC)
ended = datetime.strptime(updated, "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ").replace(tzinfo=UTC)
```

(`UTC` is already imported at `src/rss_server.py:171`; `datetime.fromisoformat`
is an equivalent alternative that handles the trailing `Z`.)

**Recommended:** Option A — a two-line change with zero behavioural effect that
resolves both findings permanently and needs no waiver bookkeeping or
line-drift maintenance.

### Option B — accept the false positive (waiver)

Record the waiver(s) on the audited item, exactly as the chore description
suggests:

```bash
python3 $(skill_path audit)/scripts/audit_waiver.py add WL-0MVYZ458V004GRF8 \
  --rule DTZ007 \
  --file /home/rgardler/projects/ContentCreator/src/rss_server.py \
  --line 2856 \
  --justification "Both stamps are explicit UTC 'Z' values parsed only to subtract one from the other; naive construction cannot cause a timezone error."
```

and a second waiver for line 2857 (sibling item `WL-0MWQYC3MZ0013YLS`).

Waiver matching requirement (verified in this intake): the waiver is matched
against the finding's `file` field byte-for-byte. Empirically `ruff check
--output-format json` reports **absolute** paths for this file whether ruff is
invoked with a relative or absolute path, so the absolute `--file` value above
is the correct one — note that `audit_waiver.py`'s `--file` help text says
"repository-relative file path", which is misleading here.

### Option C — take no action

Close with no waiver and no code change. Not recommended: the finding returns
on every audit run and generates the chore again.

## Constraints

- **Cross-repo split.** The code lives in `/home/rgardler/projects/ContentCreator`;
  work items live in `/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub/.worklog`. Any code
  commit must be made in the ContentCreator worktree.
- **Audit tier may not accept waivers** — route (B) requires the producer to
  make (or explicitly authorise) the decision.
- **No change to the console line.** Job ids, outcomes, elapsed seconds, counts
  and file names keep their current format (`src/rss_server.py:2902-2930`).
- **The project's own lint selection is not the source of the finding.** The
  audit invokes `ruff check --isolated --select DTZ007`; ContentCreator's
  `ruff.toml` only sets `extend-exclude`. Fixing this does not require touching
  `ruff.toml`, and a `per-file-ignores` entry is explicitly *not* proposed (it
  would suppress quiet future genuine DTZ007 findings).

## Existing state

- `src/rss_server.py:2845-2860` — `_job_elapsed_seconds()`:

  ```python
  created = job.get("created_at")
  updated = job.get("updated_at")
  if not isinstance(created, str) or not isinstance(updated, str):
      return None
  try:
      started = datetime.strptime(created, "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")   # 2856
      ended = datetime.strptime(updated, "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")     # 2857
  except ValueError:
      return None
  return max(0.0, (ended - started).total_seconds())
  ```

- Every writer of these stamps uses `datetime.now(UTC).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")`
  (`src/rss_server.py:2975, 6190, 6966, 7197`; also `src/podcast_version.py:52`),
  so the values genuinely are UTC and attaching `tzinfo=UTC` is factually
  correct, not a linter appeasement.
- The only consumer is `src/rss_server.py:2916`, which formats the value as
  `f"{elapsed:.1f}s"` for the terminal job log line.
- `ruff --version` in the checkout: 0.16.0; reproduction confirmed:
  `ruff check --isolated --select DTZ007 src/rss_server.py` → two DTZ007 hits
  (2856, 2857).
- Audited parent item `WL-0MVYZ458V004GRF8` (epic, `needsProducerReview: true`)
  currently has **no** recorded waivers (`audit_waiver.py list` → none), and the
  audit report's remediation loop lists this chore and the 2857 sibling.
- Existing tests already assert the console line: `tests/test_rss_regenerate.py:1133,1172`,
  `tests/test_rss_process_notes.py:708`, `tests/test_rss_regenerate_all.py:1279`,
  `tests/test_rss_llm.py:1256`.

## Desired change

One recorded producer decision plus its application: either UTC-aware parsing
in `_job_elapsed_seconds()` (Option A) or two recorded audit waivers
(Option B) — with the sibling line-2857 item resolved by the same action.

## Key Files

- `/home/rgardler/projects/ContentCreator/src/rss_server.py` — `_job_elapsed_seconds()`
  (lines 2845-2860); the two flagged `strptime` calls at 2856 and 2857; consumer
  at 2916.
- `/home/rgardler/projects/ContentCreator/tests/test_rss_regenerate.py` — asserts
  the "complete in <elapsed>s" console line; extend if route (b) needs an extra
  assertion.
- `/home/rgardler/projects/ContentCreator/tests/test_rss_process_notes.py`,
  `tests/test_rss_regenerate_all.py`, `tests/test_rss_llm.py` — same console-line
  assertions, regression surface for the elapsed value.
- `/home/rgardler/projects/ContentCreator/ruff.toml` — project lint config
  (read-only context; not expected to change).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Waiver may silently fail to match (route B).** Waivers compare the finding's
  `file` string exactly; the audit reports absolute paths. Mitigation: verify
  with `audit_waiver.py list WL-0MVYZ458V004GRF8` plus a re-scan before closing.
- **Line-pinned waivers drift.** A waiver scoped to line 2856 stops matching if
  code above it shifts. Omitting `--line` would accept DTZ007 for the whole file
  and hide future genuine findings — line-specific is preferred.
- **Assumption:** stamps are always UTC "…Z" values, as every writer uses
  `datetime.now(UTC)`. Non-conforming input already falls back to `None` and must
  keep doing so.
- **Scope-creep risk:** the audit's round-2 sibling finding (line 2857) is the
  only adjacent one; any further DTZ findings elsewhere in ContentCreator should
  be filed as linked work items, not folded into this chore.
- **Framework defect noted, not fixed here:** `audit_waiver.py`'s `--file` help
  says "repository-relative" while findings carry absolute paths. This lives in
  the agent framework (`~/.pi/agent/skills/audit`), outside this repository's
  boundaries — record it as a separate SorraAgents work item rather than editing
  framework code from this task.

## Related work

- **WL-0MVYZ458V004GRF8** — parent/audited epic (Standup→podcast pipeline);

## Appendix: Clarifying questions and answers

- **Q1 — Which route for this finding?** (a) fix the code so both `strptime`

  `audit_waiver.py add` on `WL-0MVYZ458V004GRF8`; (c) no action.

# ruff DTZ007: naive datetime in `_job_elapsed_seconds` (rss_server.py:2856-2857)

## Problem

Ruff reports DTZ007 — "Naive datetime constructed using `datetime.datetime.strptime()` without `%z`" — on two adjacent lines in `rss_server.py` (`_job_elapsed_seconds` function). The function parses `created_at` / `updated_at` ISO-8601 UTC timestamps to compute wall-clock elapsed seconds. Both datetimes are naive but represent the same UTC epoch, so the subtraction produces correct elapsed seconds. However, the code is inconsistent with the project's broader use of tz-aware datetimes.

## Users

- **Producer / audit system**: needs a consistent decision on whether this narrow, safe pattern is accepted as a false positive (record waiver) or fixed.
- **Future maintainers**: would benefit from consistent datetime handling (tz-aware throughout).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Producer accepts one of two paths:
   - **Option A — Accept as false positive:** Record an audit waiver via `audit_waiver.py add <audited-item-id> --rule DTZ007 --file src/rss_server.py --justification "…"`. A waiver with no `--line` would cover both lines (2856 and 2857) and prevents re-creation of chores.
   - **Option B — Fix the code:** Replace `strptime` with tz-aware parsing (preferred: `.fromisoformat(dt_str.replace("Z", "+00:00"))` consistent with existing pattern at line 2216) **or** add `.replace(tzinfo=UTC)` post-parse.
2. If Option B is chosen, apply the same fix to the sibling work item for line 2856 (WL-0MWQYC2ZQ002NGZP), or combine into a single fix.
3. The ruff check `ruff check --isolated --select DTZ007 src/rss_server.py` passes (zero errors) after resolution.

## Impact

Ruff DTZ007 false-positive decision: accept the narrow elapsed-time pattern as a waiver (no code change) or fix the two datetime parses to use tz-aware ISO timestamps, improving consistency with the rest of the project.

## Constraints

- The fix must not change the function's return value (elapsed seconds in float).
- If fixing, the approach must be consistent with the project's existing datetime handling pattern (see line 2216).
- The sibling item (line 2856) shares the same function and should be resolved in the same change.

## Existing state

# Problem

`wl delete` and `wl undelete` run an auto-sync after a successful mutation, but that internal sync does not forward the project's `syncAllowedAuthors` allow-list to the author-identity gate. The gate therefore runs in *strict* mode and refuses any incoming commit whose author is not the local `user.email` — even when the project explicitly allow-lists that identity for `wl sync`.

Observed 2026-11-22 in the SorraAgents store (`.worklog/config.yaml` allow-lists `sorra@thewizardscode.com`):

```
$ wl delete SA-0MWRDN7TC003VLD0 --reason "..." --json
{"success": true, ...}
Warning: auto-sync after delete failed: Refusing to merge worklog data from
refs/worklog/remotes/origin/worklog/data: 1 incoming commit(s) fail the
author-identity gate.
- db2108e72b: author email 'sorra@thewizardscode.com' does not match configured
  user.email '250240+SorraTheOrc@users.noreply.github.com'
```

A subsequent explicit `wl sync` in the same checkout merged the same batch without complaint and pushed successfully — proving the allow-list is correct and only the auto-sync path is at fault.

# Root cause

`src/commands/delete.ts` (~line 298) and `src/commands/undelete.ts` (~line 411) both do:

```ts
const defaults = getSyncDefaults(config || undefined);
await performSync(dataPath, utils.getDatabase, {
  ...
  gitRemote: defaults.gitRemote,
  gitBranch: defaults.gitBranch,
  // allowForeignAuthor / allowedAuthors never forwarded
});
```

`getSyncDefaults()` returns `allowedAuthors` (and the derived `allowForeignAuthor`), but neither field is passed into `performSync`. The CLI `wl sync` command (`src/commands/sync.ts` ~line 779–804) does forward both, which is why explicit syncs honour the allow-list and auto-syncs do not.

# Consequence

Every `wl delete`/`wl undelete` performed while the remote carries commits from an allow-listed non-local identity prints a scary warning and silently leaves the mutation unpushed. If the operator never runs an explicit `wl sync`, the deletion can be resurrected by a later pull, and agent sessions that assume "delete ⇒ propagated" are misled. It also produces confusing incident noise that looks like an identity misconfiguration.

# Users

- **Operators** using `wl delete`/`wl undelete`: mutations should propagate without a manual follow-up sync, and no spurious identity-gate warning.
- **Agents** running delete/undelete in a worklog-authenticated checkout: their mutation must not be stranded behind a gate that ignores the project's own allow-list.

# Acceptance Criteria

- `wl delete` auto-sync forwards `allowedAuthors` (and `allowForeignAuthor`) from `getSyncDefaults()` into `performSync`, so a commit authored by an allow-listed identity merges without refusal.
- `wl undelete` auto-sync forwards the same fields, with identical semantics.
- Strict mode is preserved: when the config has no allow-list (or `syncAllowedAuthors: []`), a foreign-author commit is still refused by delete/undelete auto-sync, and the existing warning is still printed on refusal.
- The empty-author-email gate is unchanged in all paths (allow-list can never admit an empty author).
- Regression tests cover delete auto-sync and undelete auto-sync: allow-listed author merges; non-allow-listed author refuses with a warning and does not abort the mutation; `--no-sync` still skips the sync entirely.
- Validation: new tests fail on the current code (gate refuses the allow-listed author) and pass after the fix.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

# Impact

Deleting or restoring a work item in a project that allow-lists a second (operator or agent) identity now propagates on its own instead of printing a false identity-gate failure and stranding the change until someone runs `wl sync` manually.

# Constraints

- Do not widen the gate: the fix forwards *the project's configured allow-list*, never an allow-all. `syncAllowedAuthors: []` must remain strict.
- Do not change `performSync`'s option contract in a way that breaks the CLI path (`src/commands/sync.ts`).
- Keep the "sync failure must not abort the delete/restore" contract: a genuine refusal still warns and leaves the local mutation intact.

# Key Files (predicted)

- `src/commands/delete.ts` — forward `allowedAuthors` / `allowForeignAuthor` from `getSyncDefaults()` into the auto-sync `performSync` call
- `src/commands/undelete.ts` — same fix for the restore auto-sync
- `tests/` (delete/undelete CLI suites) — regression coverage for allow-listed vs strict authors
- `docs/SYNC_IDENTITY_GATE.md` — note that delete/undelete auto-sync honours the same allow-list

# Related work

- WL-0MTGDW58X007UJDS — Replace binary author-identity gate with configurable author whitelist (origin of `syncAllowedAuthors`)
- WL-0MVMZP6A5005PB66 — wl sync blocked: identity gate refuses 7 commits authored by sorra@thewizardscode.com (the incident that allow-listed this identity for explicit syncs)
